= CHERIoT memory subsystem: FPV testplan
:toc: left
:toclevels: 2
:sectnums:
:imagesdir: figures

This testplan turns every requirement of the CHERIoT memory subsystem (`cheriot_mem_sys`) into
testpoints for formal property verification (FPV). For each testpoint it gives the rule as a
formula, the checks, every case the tool must be shown to reach, the edge cases, and what must never
happen. It covers the whole subsystem: the tag path with the WTRC, the meta SRAM access, the
revocation engine, the registers, the interrupt and the alert. The requirements, the assumptions
and the open questions for the designers are in the
xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc[design architecture]; the three checkers that
run the testpoints, with their environments and contracts, are in the
xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc[TB architecture].

== Overview

=== How to read this testplan

*Rule:* FPV does not run tests. The tool tries every input sequence the environment allows, so a
testpoint states the rule and the cases the tool must be shown to reach, not a configuration to
run.

A software testplan picks configurations and checks the result. This testplan keeps its method and
changes its form:

[cols="3,5",options="header"]
|===
|In a software testplan |In this FPV testplan

|Choose a configuration, run it, observe |The tool tries every configuration at once. A cover shows
that the configuration you care about is reached
|Vary one parameter, hold the rest |One cover per value of that parameter, the others held: the
*Cases* table of a testpoint
|Exercise the full truth table of the conditions |One cover per row; one assertion of the formula
checks every row at once: the *Truth table*
|Randomise values |Free inputs: the tool tries every value, not a sample
|Expected result as a formula |The same formula, in the *Rule* line, checked by an assertion in both
directions
|Edge cases, with steps |Covers on boundary values (*Edge cases*); the assertion already checks them
|"Not directly observable" |Often observable here: the checks sit on the subsystem's ports, e.g.
every read the engine makes on `tbre_tl_h`
|===

Every testpoint has the same parts, in this order; a part with nothing to say is left out:

[cols="1,5",options="header"]
|===
|Part |Holds

|Requirements |the `REQ_*` rows the testpoint closes; each requirement is in exactly one testpoint
|Rule |the expected behaviour as a formula over the definitions
|Observed at |the ports where the checks look
|Checks |the assertions, each named by what it guarantees, with its direction
|Cases |covers, each named by the situation it reaches; one input varied at a time from a base
case, each with the expected outcome
|Truth table |covers, one per row of the rule's conditions; the family of covers has one name
|Edge cases |covers on boundary values: first and last of a range, seams, collisions in one cycle
|Never |what must never happen: the negative space
|Run |the environment of the run that checks it (run variants), and why
|Blocked by |the open questions an expected value depends on
|===

In running text a check or case name is in italics, after its testpoint when it belongs to another
one: `tf_forward` _no extra host request_. Checks and cases had numbers before (A1, C1); the
former ids table maps each former number to its name.

[cols="1,2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Kind |Type |Meaning

|forward |assertion |whenever the rule says the design must act, it acts: stimulus implies
response, within the stated time
|backward |assertion |the design acts only when the rule says so: response implies stimulus. A
one-bit credit, set by the stimulus and used up by the response, catches a response with no
stimulus and a second response to one stimulus
|case |cover |a case the tool must show is reachable. An unreachable cover means every assertion
about that case proves nothing (it is *vacuous*)
|===

* Every expected value comes from a formula and a spec citation, never from the RTL. Numbers in
  examples are Earl Grey's, computed with a script from the formulas. The proofs bind the design
  with Earl Grey's parameters (TB architecture, How the checkers are built), so every result holds
  for that configuration; another configuration reruns the same testplan with its values.
* An assertion holds for every legal input; the covers prove that the inputs that matter are among
  them. Both are needed: an assertion without its covers can pass because nothing happened.

*Status:* draft.

== Definitions and algebra

Every rule in this testplan is a formula over the definitions below, so the expected value of
every case can be computed and checked by hand. Each definition cites its source. Values are Earl
Grey's ([IF] Parameters). Formulas use `and`, `or`, `not`; `a` is a byte address; `x >> n` and
`x & m` are the usual shift and mask.

=== Addresses and regions

*Rule:* a byte address finds its capability tag and its revocation bit from its offset in its
region: bits 2:0 pick the byte inside the 8-byte capability, bits 7:3 the bit inside a 32-bit meta
word, the bits above the word ([ToO] Metadata Encoding: one bit covers "one 8-byte capability" or
"8 heap bytes", one word "256 bytes").

.Fields of an address's offset in its region, for tags and for revocation bits
image::cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan_figures.svg#fig2[Offset fields,align=center,width=760,height=56]

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Field |Use

|offset bits 2:0 |byte in the 8-byte capability: all 8 bytes share one tag and one revocation bit
|offset bits 7:3 |bit select inside the meta word (the tag order is open question Q2; the bitmap's is given: "bit `b` of word `w` covers the eight heap bytes starting at `MainSramBaseAddr + (w * 32 + b) * 8`{empty}", [ToO])
|offset bits 31:8 |word index: meta word address = table base + 4 × index
|===

[cols="2,4,4",options="header"]
|===
|Name |Definition |Source

|`MainSram(a)` |`0x1000_0000 \<= a < 0x1003_0000` |[IF] `MainSramBaseAddr` (inclusive),
`MainSramTopAddr` (exclusive): the 128 KiB main SRAM and the 64 KiB second SRAM
|`Nvm(a)` |`0x3000_0000 \<= a < 0x3020_0000` |[IF] `NvmBaseAddr`, `NvmTopAddr`
|`Tagged(a)` |`MainSram(a) or Nvm(a)` |[ToO] Tag Filter: "memory capable of holding
capabilities"; [ToO] Revocation Engine: "a tagged region"
|`Revocable(a)` |`MainSram(a)` |[PG]: "capabilities whose base lies outside the main SRAM region
are never revoked"; [ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map: "Main SRAM revocation bitmap"
|`RBase(a)`, `RTop(a)` |base and top (exclusive) of the tagged region holding `a` |[IF]
|`Cap(a)` |`a & ~7`: the capability that holds byte `a` |[ToO] Metadata Encoding
|`TagWord(a)` |`0x1100_0000 + T + 4 * ((a - RBase(a)) >> 8)`, with `T` = `0x8C00` in the main SRAM
and `0x0C00` in the NVM |[ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map; [ToO] Metadata Encoding
|`TagBit(a)` |`((a - RBase(a)) >> 3) & 31` |gap, raised with the designers
|`RevWord(a)` |`0x1100_0000 + 4 * ((a - 0x1000_0000) >> 8)`, for `Revocable(a)` |[ToO] Meta SRAM
Address Map, `revbm` window
|`RevBit(a)` |`((a - 0x1000_0000) >> 3) & 31` |[ToO] (as above)
|===

Worked numbers, computed from the formulas (tag bits assume the order asked in Q2):

[cols="2,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|Address |`TagWord`, `TagBit` |`RevWord`, `RevBit`

|`0x1000_0000`, first capability of the main SRAM |`0x1100_8C00`, 0 |`0x1100_0000`, 0
|`0x1000_1238` and `0x1000_123C`, one capability |`0x1100_8C48`, 7 |-
|`0x1000_1240`, the next capability |`0x1100_8C48`, 8 |-
|`0x1000_4000` to `0x1000_4007`, one granule |- |`0x1100_0100`, 0
|`0x1000_4008` |- |`0x1100_0100`, 1
|`0x1001_FFF8`, last capability of the 128 KiB main SRAM |`0x1100_93FC`, 31 |-
|`0x1002_0000`, first capability of the second SRAM |`0x1100_9400`, 0 |-
|`0x1002_FFF8`, last capability of the region |`0x1100_97FC`, 31 |`0x1100_0BFC`, 31
|`0x3000_0000`, first NVM capability |`0x1100_0C00`, 0 |not revocable
|`0x3000_0400` |`0x1100_0C10`, 0 |not revocable
|`0x301F_FFF8`, last NVM capability |`0x1100_8BFC`, 31 |not revocable
|===

* The tables end where the next one starts: main SRAM tags at `0x1100_9800` (the meta SRAM top),
  NVM tags at `0x1100_8C00`, the bitmap at `0x1100_0C00`.
* The seam between the main SRAM and the second SRAM, at `0x1002_0000`, is inside one region: both
  sides are tagged and revocable, and their tags sit in consecutive words.

*Status:* draft; tag bits gap, raised with the designers.

=== Requests and responses

*Rule:* each rule of the testplan reads a request or a response through these predicates. A
request `r` arrives on `cored_tl_d` with the tag sideband `cored_tag_h2d`; on the other ports it
has no sideband.

[cols="2,4,4",options="header"]
|===
|Name |Definition |Source

|`Ena` |`cheriot_ena_i == MuBi4True` (`4'h6`); any of the other 15 values is ePMP mode
|[ToO] Access Checkers: "any `cheriot_ena_i` value other than a strict `MuBi4True` - including a
strict `MuBi4False`{empty}"; [HJSON] `INTERSIG.MUBI`
|`Get(r)`, `PutFull(r)`, `PutPartial(r)` |`a_opcode` is `Get`, `PutFullData`, `PutPartialData`
|[TLUL] opcode table
|`Wr(r)` |`PutFull(r) or PutPartial(r)` |[TLUL]
|`Hint(r)` |`Get(r) and cored_tag_h2d`: the capability-load hint |[CIBEX] `data_tag_o`; [LSU]:
"Also driven high on both beats of a capability load"
|`TagIn(r)` |`cored_tag_h2d` of a write: the tag to write |[IF] `cored_tag_h2d`
|`W0(r)`, `W1(r)` |address bit 2 is 0 (lower word, the capability's address), or 1 (upper word, its metadata) |[ToO] WTRC: "W0 at the lower and then W1 at the upper address"; [LSU]: "low word,
then high word"
|`NvmCapStore(r)` |`Ena and Wr(r) and Nvm(a) and TagIn(r)` |[ToO] WTRC: "a write in strict CHERIoT
mode to the NVM with the tag sideband set"
|`Lookup(r)` |`Ena and Tagged(a) and ((Get(r) and Hint(r) and W0(r)) or Wr(r)) and not
NvmCapStore(r)` |[ToO] Tag Filter: "A meta lookup is needed when ..."
|`FullWord(r)` |`a_size == 2` at a word-aligned address. TL-UL then sets all four `a_mask` bits
|[ToO] Access Checkers; [TLPC] `sizeMatchesMask`, `addrSizeAligned`
|`Legal(p, r)` |`Ena and InRegion(p, a) and FullWord(r) and (Get(r) or PutFull(r))` |[ToO] Access
Checkers; the design architecture's "legal request"
|`InRegion(p, a)` |tag port: `0x1100_0C00 \<= a < 0x1100_9800`; `corerevbm_tl`, `revbm_tl_d` and
the TBRE's bitmap port: `0x1100_0000 \<= a < 0x1100_0C00` |[ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map, "Reachable
from"
|`Malformed(s)` |a response `s` whose `d_opcode` is not the one its request needs (`AccessAckData` for a `Get`, `AccessAck` for a write), or whose `d_size` differs from the request's `a_size`
|[TLPC] `respOpcode`, `d_size`: the response "must have the same size as the original request";
[HJSON] `sweep_err`: "malformed"
|`IntgOk(s)` |the response integrity and the data integrity of `s` match its fields |[TLUL] Usage
of User Bits
|`FullPut(w)` |capability store word `w` is a `PutFullData` with every `a_mask` bit set |[ToO]
Error Handling: a partial capability store is a fault (`REQ_WTRC_10`)
|`InSeq(w)` |`w` is a W0 presented while no capability store is open, or the W1 presented as the
next capability store after its W0 |[ToO] WTRC: W0 then W1 (`REQ_WTRC_10`)
|`Faulty(w)` |`not FullPut(w) or not InSeq(w)`, or `w` has a bad command or data integrity, or
`not IntgOk(w'{empty}s NVM answer)` |[ToO] Error Handling (`REQ_WTRC_10`)
|`NvmOk(w)` |the NVM answer of `w` has no `d_error` |[ToO] WTRC answer table
|===

* `a_source` grows at each arbiter: a request's `a_source` `s` leaves input `i` as `(s << 1) | i`
  at the 2:1 tag arbiter and `(s << 2) | i` at the 4:1 arbiter, kept to 8 bits; the answer comes
  back with the added bits shifted off ([TLUL] Source ID growth). Example: `0x15` on input 2 of the
  4:1 arbiter leaves as `0x56`; the answer `0x56` returns to input 2 as `0x15`.
* Requesters keep the top bits of `a_source` free for that growth (A9): one bit at the 2:1 tag
  arbiter, two at the 4:1 arbiter.

*Status:* draft.

[[defs_capability]]
=== Capabilities

A capability is 64 bits plus its tag: the word at the 8-byte-aligned address `c` holds its
address, the word at `c + 4` its metadata ([ISA] §7.3, "the lower 32-bits (the capability
address)"; [LSU]: a capability store writes the "low word, then high word"). The engine decides
revocation from the base and the permissions, so the testbench decodes both from the ISA, never with
an RTL function. The design architecture states the same terms for the designers, with their ISA
citations (xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc#capability_terms[design
architecture, capability terms]); this section gives the formulas the testbench computes.

==== Capability fields

*Rule:* the metadata word holds the permissions `p`, the object type, the exponent `E` and the
bounds fields `T` and `B` ([ISA] §7.12, Figure 7.2, PDF page 62).

.Capability format, [ISA] Figure 7.2 (PDF page 62): the metadata word above, the address word below
image::cheriot_isa_fig7_2_capability_format.png[CHERIoT capability format,align=center]

[cols="2,2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Field |Bits of W1 (metadata) |Meaning

|`R` |31 |reserved
|`p` |30:25 |compressed permissions (<<defs_sealing>>)
|`otype` |24:22 |object type; not 0 means *sealed*
|`E` |21:18 |exponent of the bounds
|`T` |17:9 |top field of the bounds
|`B` |8:0 |base field of the bounds
|`a` |W0, all 32 bits |the address
|===

*Status:* draft.

'''

==== Base

*Rule:* `Base(c)` is the decoded base, from the address `a` and the fields `E`, `B` ([ISA] §7.13.3,
PDF pages 69-70; Sail `getCapBoundsBits`, PDF pages 149-150).

[cols="1,4,3",options="header"]
|===
|Step |Formula |Sail, verbatim

|1 |`e = 24` if `E == 15`, else `e = E` |`let E = if c.cE == 0xf then cap_max_E_bits`
|2 |`a_mid = (a >> e) & 0x1FF`; `a_top = a >> (e + 9)` |`let a_mid = truncate(a >> E, cap_mantissa_width)`
|3 |`c_b = -1` if `a_mid < B`, else `c_b = 0` |`let a_hi = if a_mid <_u c.B then 1 else 0`; `let
c_b = 0 - a_hi`
|4 |`Base(c) = (((a_top + c_b) << (e + 9)) \| (B << e)) mod 2^32^` |`let base : CapAddrBits =
truncate((a_top + c_b) @ c.B @ zeros(E), cap_addr_width)`
|===

Worked examples, computed from the steps:

[cols="3,2,2,1,1,1,2",options="header"]
|===
|Capability |W0 (`a`) |W1 |`E` |`B` |`c_b` |`Base`

|64-byte object, address 16 bytes in |`0x1000_4010` |`0x7E00_8000` |0 |`0x000` |0 |`0x1000_4000`
|64-byte object across a 512-byte line, address before the line |`0x1000_41F8` |`0x7E00_61F0` |0
|`0x1F0` |0 |`0x1000_41F0`
|the same object, address after the line |`0x1000_4210` |`0x7E00_61F0` |0 |`0x1F0` |-1
|`0x1000_41F0`
|object with 16-byte granular bounds |`0x1000_4100` |`0x7E10_4000` |4 |`0x000` |0 |`0x1000_4000`
|root capability |`0x0000_0000` |`0x7E3E_0000` |15 |`0x000` |0 |`0x0000_0000`
|===

* Rows 2 and 3 are one capability: the correction `c_b` gives the same base from two addresses.
  The base `0x1000_41F0` has revocation bit 30 of word `0x1100_0104`; the address `0x1000_4210`
  lies in another granule, bit 2 of word `0x1100_0108`. Revocation follows the base ([ISA] §7.8:
  "the revocation bit corresponding to the base address of the capability (N.B. not the
  address)").
* The granule of the base is `Base(c) & ~7` ([ISA] CLC Sail: `align_down(log2_revocation_granule_size,
  base)`, with granule size 8): a base anywhere in an 8-byte granule uses that granule's bit.
* Every bit pattern decodes; the ISA gives no rule for a tagged capability with malformed bounds
  ([ISA] PDF pages 70, 154-155), so the engine is checked on the decoded base alone.

*Status:* draft.

'''

[[defs_sealing]]
==== Sealing capability

*Rule:* a capability is a *sealing capability* when its permissions are in the sealing format and
grant SE, US or U0 ([ISA] CLC, PDF page 114, Sail: `let isSealingCap = cr.permit_seal |
cr.permit_unseal | cr.perm_user0`).

[cols="2,2,1,4",options="header"]
|===
|`p` (bits 5:0) |Format |`Sealing(c)` |Note

|`G 11xxx` |memory, capability read-write |0 |`G` is the global bit; it never matters here
|`G 101xx` |memory, capability read-only |0 |
|`G 10000` |memory, capability write-only |0 |
|`G 100xx`, `xx` not `00` |memory, data only |0 |
|`G 01xxx` |executable |0 |
|`G 00` U0 SE US, not all 0 |sealing |1 |any one of U0, SE, US is enough
|`G 00000` |no permissions, in the sealing format |0 |gap, raised with the designers ([ISA] §7.13.8: "may also behave unexpectedly with respect to revocation")
|===

* `Sealing(c) = (p[4:3] == 0) and (p[2:0] != 0)`.
* *Sealing* is not *sealed*. A sealed capability (`otype` not 0) of a memory format is not a sealing
  capability, so it is revoked like any other ([ISA] §7.13.2: "0 unsealed ... 9-15 non-executable
  capability sealed with given otype"; the CLC exemption tests the permissions only).

*Status:* draft; no-permission row gap, raised with the designers.

'''

==== Revoked

*Rule:* a swept capability `c` is *revoked* when `Tag(c) and not Sealing(c) and Revocable(Base(c))
and (RevSet(c) or LookupFail(c))` ([ToO] Revocation Engine: "a tagged capability that is not a
sealing capability and whose base has its revocation bit set is revoked, and so is one whose bitmap
lookup fails"; [PG]).

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Term |Definition

|`Tag(c)` |the tag the engine's tag filter returns with the words of `c`
|`RevSet(c)` |bit `RevBit(Base(c))` of the word the engine's bitmap lookup for `c` returned
|`LookupFail(c)` |that lookup was answered with `d_error`, failed `IntgOk`, or was `Malformed`
|===

In plain words: only a tagged, non-sealing capability whose base lies in the main SRAM can be
revoked, and it is revoked when its base's bit is set or the bit cannot be read. The
<<tp_tbre_decision,decision testpoint>> walks every combination.

*Status:* draft.

'''

[[defs_sweep]]
=== Sweep, status and watch

*Rule:* a sweep, its status registers and the core write watch are defined by these terms ([ToO]
Revocation Engine; [HJSON] registers; the design architecture's revocation engine terms).

[cols="2,5,3",options="header"]
|===
|Name |Definition |Source

|`TakenStart` |a write of 1 to `TBRE_START` while `TBRE_REGWEN == 1`, with `Ena and NUM != 0 and
Tagged(BASE)` |[ToO]: "starts a sweep ... if"
|`IgnoredStart` |a write of 1 to `TBRE_START` while `TBRE_REGWEN == 1`, not a `TakenStart` |[ToO]:
"Any other start is ignored"
|`BASE`, `NUM` |`TBRE_BASE_ADDR` (bits 2:0 read as 0) and `TBRE_NUM_CAPS` at the start |[HJSON]
|`N` |`min(NUM, (RTop(BASE) - BASE) / 8)` |[ToO]: "the engine sweeps `min(TBRE_NUM_CAPS, (top - TBRE_BASE_ADDR) / 8)` capabilities"
|`Swept` |the capabilities `BASE + 8k`, `0 \<= k < N` |[ToO]
|`Active` |`TBRE_REGWEN == 0` |[ToO]: "While the engine is active ... `TBRE_REGWEN` is low"
|`Resolved(c)` |proposed: both words of `c` read and answered, its bitmap lookup answered, its clear
answered |gap, raised with the designers
|`Watch(c)` |from the cycle the read of `c`{empty}'s W0 is presented on the engine's read port, in
front of its TRVK filter, until the cycle before its clear is presented on the engine's clear port
|[ToO]: "The watch starts when ..."; the ports: DV reading, Q40
|`Stale(c)` |from the cycle `c`{empty}'s clear is presented on the engine's clear port until the cycle
before it reaches the RMW filter; from then until it is accepted the clear is *held* |[ToO]:
"From the presentation of the clear until it reaches the RMW filter"; "Once the clear is at the
RMW filter ... holds it there" (checker 3 uarch D43)
|`Touch(w, c)` |a core write `w` presented on `cored_tl_d`, or accepted there and not yet answered,
with `Cap(w.a) == c` |[ToO]: "every write the core presents ... and every write it accepted there
until the write is answered"; "at capability granularity"
|===

Worked numbers for `N`, computed from the formula:

[cols="2,2,2,4",options="header"]
|===
|`BASE` |`NUM` |`N` |What it shows

|`0x1001_FFF0` |4 |4 |crosses the seam to the second SRAM at `0x1002_0000`
|`0x1002_FFF0` |5 |2 |clipped at the region top `0x1003_0000`
|`0x1002_FFF8` |1 |1 |last capability of the main SRAM region
|`0x1000_0000` |`0x7FFF_FFFF` |`0x6000` |the whole main SRAM region, 24,576 capabilities
|`0x3000_0000` |`0x7FFF_FFFF` |`0x4_0000` |the whole NVM, 262,144 capabilities
|`0x301F_F5F8` |1 |1 |last capability below the emulated OTP pages ([PG]: "from `0x301F_F600` in Earl Grey")
|`0x1003_0000`, `0x0FFF_FFF8`, `0x2FFF_FFF8`, `0x3020_0000` |1 |- |outside the tagged regions:
ignored start
|`0x1000_0000` |0 |- |ignored start
|===

*Status:* draft; `Resolved` gap, raised with the designers.

[[checker1]]
== Checker 1: tag path

Checker 1 holds the real tag path from `cored_tl_d` to the RMW filter's downstream port: the core's
tag filter with its WTRC, the 2:1 tag arbiter, the tag clear squash and the RMW filter
(xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#tag_path[TB architecture, checker 1]). The TBRE's
tag requests at arbiter input 1 and the meta SRAM answers at the RMW filter's downstream port are
driven by the testbench.

=== Tag filter

==== How it works

*Rule:* [ToO] Tag Filter, "The tag filter forks each core data access into up to three streams,
the host port, the meta port, and a small metadata FIFO ... After receiving the responses, the
streams are joined together and the data response is returned to the core."

* Every core request goes to the host port (`cored_tl_h`) and leaves a FIFO entry: read, lookup,
  aligned. A request with `Lookup(r)` also goes to the meta port, with the meta word, the bit
  select and, for a write, the tag to write.
* The answer to the core waits for every part it needs: the host answer always, the meta answer
  when a lookup was made. Both directions pass in the cycle they are presented ([ToO] Timing).
* The tag of a capability load is looked up with W0, returned with W0 and captured, then returned
  with W1 and cleared. A write answer is untagged and leaves the capture alone.
* The meta answer goes into a buffer one entry deeper than the FIFO, so the meta port never refuses
  an answer: two tag filters share the RMW filter, and a refused answer could deadlock them.
* Full explanation, with worked examples and waveforms: design architecture, section "Tag filter".

'''

[[tp_tf_forward]]
==== tf_forward: every access forwarded once, unchanged, with its answer

*Requirements:* `REQ_TF_01a`, `REQ_TF_01b`, `REQ_TF_01c`, `REQ_TF_07`, `REQ_TF_16a`, `REQ_TF_16b`.

*Rule:* every core request `r` that is not an `NvmCapStore` appears once on `cored_tl_h` with
every A-channel field of `r`, in the first cycle `r` is presented; the answer to `r` on `cored_tl_d`
carries the host answer's `d_opcode`, `d_size`, `d_source`, `d_data` and data integrity (and its
response integrity when no meta error is merged in), in the cycle its last part arrives.

*Observed at:* `cored_tl_d` and `cored_tl_h`, both channels.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|forwarded unchanged |forward |a request presented on `cored_tl_d` and not yet forwarded is
presented on `cored_tl_h` in the same cycle, with the same A-channel fields (`REQ_TF_01b`,
`REQ_TF_16a`)
|no extra host request |backward |a request presented on `cored_tl_h` belongs to a core request
presented and not yet forwarded: no request invented (`REQ_TF_01c`), none forwarded twice
(`REQ_TF_01a`). Checked when presented, not only when accepted: stronger, and the same rule
|answer has host fields |forward |the answer's fields equal the host answer's (`REQ_TF_07`)
|answer on last part |forward |the answer is presented in the cycle its last part (host answer, meta answer if a lookup was made) arrives, and not before (`REQ_TF_16b`)
|accepted after forwarded |forward |a core request is accepted only once its host request has
been taken, in that cycle or before: none is lost (`REQ_TF_01a`)
|===

.Cases
[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Request or timing

|Get to SRAM |`Get` of the main SRAM, not hinted
|plain store to NVM |`PutFullData` to the NVM with tag 0
|byte store to SRAM |`PutPartialData` of one byte to the main SRAM
|Get to peripheral |`Get` of a peripheral, outside both tagged regions
|W1 while W0 open |two requests outstanding: W0 and W1 of a capability load
|host port stalls |the host port stalls (`a_ready` = 0) while the meta port takes the lookup
|meta port stalls |the meta port stalls while the host port takes the request
|meta answer first |an answer whose meta part arrives before its host part
|host answer first |an answer whose host part arrives before its meta part
|both parts together |an answer whose meta and host parts arrive in one cycle
|===

*Edge cases:* _host answer error_, the host answers with `d_error`; _back to back_, requests in
consecutive cycles; _request in answer cycle_, the second request presented in the cycle the first
is answered.

*Never:* a request on `cored_tl_h` the core did not present; a second one for the same core
request; a core request accepted but never forwarded; a changed address, opcode, size, mask, data,
`a_source` or `a_user`; an answer before its last part arrived, or one cycle after.

*Run:* V1. Capability stores to the NVM are excluded: their host request is a `Get` (`wtrc_store`).

*Blocked by:* Q12 for _no extra host request_: the check assumes the core holds a request until it
is accepted (assumption A1).

'''

[[tp_tf_lookup]]
==== tf_lookup: when a tag is looked up

*Requirements:* `REQ_TF_02`, `REQ_TF_03`, `REQ_TF_04`, `REQ_TF_17`.

*Rule:* a request issues exactly one meta request if `Lookup(r)`, and none otherwise.

*Observed at:* `cored_tl_d` (the request) and the tag filter's meta port (input 0 of the 2:1 tag
arbiter).

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|lookup carries valid integrity |forward |every lookup presented on the port carries a valid command integrity (`REQ_TF_17`; nothing else checks it: the TL-UL ABVIP leaves every integrity field free)
|lookup in same cycle |forward |a request presented with `Lookup(r)` whose lookup is not yet
taken has its meta request presented, in the same cycle
|no unneeded lookup |backward |a meta request presented belongs to a request presented with
`Lookup(r)` whose lookup is not yet taken: none without a lookup, at most one per request
|===

Both checks hold while no WTRC tag write is owed (`wtrc_compare`): an owed tag write goes to the
meta port ahead of any lookup ([ToO] WTRC), so the lookup waits for it. Under assumption A4 nothing
is presented then, and a core that breaks assumption A4 is out of scope (not covered).

.Cases: one input varied from the base case, hinted W0 Get
[cols="2,2,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Varied |Request |`Lookup`

|hinted W0 Get |none: the base case |CHERIoT mode, `Get` `0x1000_1238`, hinted |1
|hinted W1 Get |address bit 2 |`Get` `0x1000_123C`, hinted (W1) |0
|unhinted Get |hint |`Get` `0x1000_1238`, not hinted |0
|word store |opcode |`PutFullData` `0x1000_1238`, tag 0 (`sw`) |1
|byte store |opcode |`PutPartialData` `0x1000_1239`, tag 0 (`sb`) |1
|capability store |opcode, tag |`PutFullData` `0x1000_1238`, tag 1 (`csc`) |1
|NVM capability load |region |`Get` `0x3000_0400`, hinted |1
|NVM capability store |region, opcode |`PutFullData` `0x3000_0400`, tag 1 |0
|NVM word store |region, opcode |`PutFullData` `0x3000_0400`, tag 0 |1
|peripheral Get |region |`Get` `0x4000_0000` (a peripheral), hinted |0
|bitmap store |region |`PutFullData` `0x1100_0100` (the bitmap window), tag 0 |0
|ePMP mode |mode |`cheriot_ena_i` = `MuBi4False` |0
|invalid mode |mode |`cheriot_ena_i` = `4'h0`, an invalid encoding |0
|===

.Truth table: one cover per cell
[cols="3,2,2,2,2",options="header"]
|===
|Access |CHERIoT mode, main SRAM |CHERIoT mode, NVM |CHERIoT mode, other address |ePMP mode
(15 values)

|`Get`, hinted, W0 |1 |1 |0 |0
|`Get`, hinted, W1 |0 |0 |0 |0
|`Get`, not hinted |0 |0 |0 |0
|write, tag 0 |1 |1 |0 |0
|write, tag 1 |1 |0: WTRC |0 |0
|===

Each cell is one cover of the _truth table cell_ family: 20 covers, one per row and column.

*Edge cases:* _region edge address_, one cover per address: the first and last capability of each
region and one capability beyond, `0x0FFF_FFF8` (0), `0x1000_0000` (1), `0x1002_FFF8` (1),
`0x1003_0000` (0), `0x2FFF_FFF8` (0), `0x3000_0000` (1), `0x301F_FFF8` (1), `0x3020_0000` (0); both
sides of the seam, `0x1001_FFF8` and `0x1002_0000` (both 1). _Every mode value_, one cover per
value: all 16 `cheriot_ena_i` values.

*Never:* a lookup in ePMP mode; for a W1 load, a plain load, a peripheral, the bitmap window, or a
capability store to the NVM; two lookups for one request.

*Run:* V1.

'''

[[tp_tf_meta_request]]
==== tf_meta_request: which word, which bit, which tag

*Requirements:* `REQ_TF_05a`, `REQ_TF_05b`, `REQ_TF_06`.

*Rule:* the meta request of `r` has `a_address = TagWord(r.a)` and bit select `TagBit(r.a)`; for a
write, the tag to write is `TagIn(r)`. A read's lookup is a read, a write's lookup a write ([ToO]
RMW Filter: "A read is forwarded ... A write is turned into a `Get` of the meta word").

*Observed at:* the tag filter's meta port.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|tag word and bit |forward |address and bit select of every meta request (`REQ_TF_05a`, `REQ_TF_05b`)
|write carries its tag |forward |tag to write of every write's meta request (`REQ_TF_06`)
|Get only for a read |forward |a read's meta request is a `Get`; a write's is not, so the RMW
filter writes its tag (`REQ_TF_06`)
|===

The checks look at the meta request of the request presented on `cored_tl_d`, while no WTRC tag
write is owed (as `tf_lookup`).

.Cases: address to meta word and bit (bit order of Q2)
[cols="2,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Request address |Meta word, bit select

|W0, bit 7 |`0x1000_1238` (W0 load or store) |`0x1100_8C48`, 7
|W1, bit 7 |`0x1000_123C` (store to W1) |`0x1100_8C48`, 7
|byte in capability |`0x1000_1239` to `0x1000_123F` (byte stores) |`0x1100_8C48`, 7
|next capability, bit 8 |`0x1000_1240` |`0x1100_8C48`, 8
|first SRAM capability |`0x1000_0000` |`0x1100_8C00`, 0
|seam |`0x1001_FFF8`, `0x1002_0000` (the seam) |`0x1100_93FC`, 31; `0x1100_9400`, 0
|last SRAM capability |`0x1002_FFF8` |`0x1100_97FC`, 31
|NVM capabilities |`0x3000_0000`, `0x3000_0400`, `0x301F_FFF8` |`0x1100_0C00`, 0; `0x1100_0C10`,
0; `0x1100_8BFC`, 31
|===

.Cases: tag to write
[cols="2,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Write |Tag

|plain store, tag 0 |`sw`, `sh`, `sb` over a capability |0
|capability store, tag 1 |`csc` of a tagged capability, both words |1
|capability store, tag 0 |`csc` of an untagged capability |0
|===

*Never:* a meta address outside `0x1100_0C00`-`0x1100_97FF`; another capability's bit select; tag 1
for a plain store.

*Run:* V1.

*Blocked by:* Q2 (bit order) for `TagBit`.

'''

[[tp_tf_sticky_tag]]
==== tf_sticky_tag: the tag returned with each answer

*Requirements:* `REQ_TF_08`, `REQ_TF_09`, `REQ_TF_10`, `REQ_TF_11a`, `REQ_TF_11b`, `REQ_TF_11c`.

*Rule:* the tag returned with the answer `s` to request `r`:

* `0` if `r` is a write (`REQ_TF_11a`); a write answer leaves the capture unchanged (`REQ_TF_11b`);
* the meta answer's tag if `Lookup(r)` and `Get(r)` (W0 of a capability load); it is also captured
  (`REQ_TF_08`; not checked when `s` has `d_error`, but captured all the same);
* the capture if `Get(r) and Hint(r) and Tagged(a) and Ena and W1(r)`; the capture is then cleared,
  which a plain read of the upper word right after the load observes: it returns 0 (`REQ_TF_09`,
  `REQ_TF_10`);
* `0` for every other read (`REQ_TF_11c`).

The capture is `0` after reset. One case is open in the spec: a plain read answered between W0 and
W1, which [ToO] ("on the following unaligned response the captured value is presented again") and
`REQ_TF_11c` read differently. The core never sends it (assumption A3), so the testplan claims
nothing for it (not covered).

*Observed at:* `cored_tag_d2h` with the answers on `cored_tl_d`.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|answer tag follows rule |forward |the tag of every answer equals the rule's value
|===

.Cases
[cols="2,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Access |Tags returned

|SRAM capability, tag 1 |`clc` from the main SRAM, stored tag 1 |1, 1
|SRAM capability, tag 0 |`clc` from the main SRAM, stored tag 0 |0, 0
|NVM capability, tag 1 |`clc` from the NVM, stored tag 1 |1, 1
|word load |`lw` of a tagged capability's word |0
|load in ePMP mode |`clc` in ePMP mode |0, 0
|peripheral load |`clc` of a peripheral address |0, 0
|store answer |a store's answer |0
|W0 error, then W1 |`clc` whose W0 answer has `d_error` |not checked, W1 returns the capture
|upper word after load |a plain `lw` of `c + 4` right after a `clc` of `c` with stored tag 1 |0:
the capture was cleared (`REQ_TF_10`)
|===

*Never:* tag 1 on a write answer, on a plain load, on a load outside the tagged regions or in ePMP
mode; a capture still returned after its W1.

*Run:* V1 for `REQ_TF_08`, `REQ_TF_09`, `REQ_TF_10`, `REQ_TF_11a`, `REQ_TF_11c`. `REQ_TF_10` is
decided on the core's tag filter by _answer tag follows rule_ through _upper word after load_:
assumption A3 constrains hinted reads only, so a plain read of the upper word right after a
capability load is legal and returns the capture, 0 once cleared. Only the precondition of
`REQ_TF_11b` is unreachable there: W1 follows W0 as the next request (assumption A3) and answers
come in order (assumption A7), so no write answer comes between W0 and W1; a core that breaks
assumption A3 is out of scope (not covered). On the engine's tag filter (`tbre_clear`) the
engine's clears share the path with its reads, so `REQ_TF_11b` may be reached in V1 there; its
covers tell.

They needed run V2, which let the core break its access order; a core that does is out of scope
since (not covered). The _upper word after load_ case reaches former A2's observable with a
legal plain read, so `REQ_TF_10` needs no variant.

'''

[[tp_tf_errors]]
==== tf_errors: errors and response integrity

*Requirements:* `REQ_TF_12a`, `REQ_TF_12b`, `REQ_TF_13`.

*Rule:* `d_error = HostErr or (Lookup(r) and MetaErr)`. When a meta error sets `d_error` on an
error-free host answer, `IntgOk(answer) == IntgOk(host answer)`.

*Observed at:* the answers on `cored_tl_d`, the host answers on `cored_tl_h`, the meta answers at
the meta port.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|error when a part has one |forward |an answer whose host answer or joined meta answer has an
error has `d_error` (`REQ_TF_12a`)
|no error without a cause |backward |an answer with `d_error` has a host answer or a joined meta
answer with an error (`REQ_TF_12b`)
|merged error keeps integrity |forward |when only the meta answer has an error, the answer's
response integrity is valid exactly when the host answer's was (`REQ_TF_13`)
|===

.Truth table: one cover per row, for a read and for a write
[cols="1,1,1,1,3",options="header"]
|===
|Host error |Lookup |Meta error |`d_error` |Response integrity

|0 |0 |- |0 |the host's
|1 |0 |- |1 |the host's
|0 |1 |0 |0 |the host's
|0 |1 |1 |1 |adjusted: valid if and only if the host's was valid (two covers: host integrity valid, broken)
|1 |1 |0 |1 |the host's
|1 |1 |1 |1 |the host's
|===

Each row is covered twice, once for a read and once for a write; row 4 is covered both with the
host integrity valid and with it broken: 14 covers of the _truth table row_ family.

*Never:* an error lost; an error invented; a broken integrity made valid; a valid integrity made
broken.

*Run:* V1. Broken integrities are legal stimulus: integrity is free on every port.

'''

[[tp_tf_flow]]
==== tf_flow: no stall, no lost answer

*Requirements:* `REQ_TF_14`, `REQ_TF_15a`, `REQ_TF_15b`.

*Rule:* the meta port's `d_ready` is 1 whenever a meta answer is offered; every request is accepted
and answered exactly once, given the host and meta ports accept and answer.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|meta answer taken |safety |meta `d_ready` is 1 in every cycle a meta answer is offered
(`REQ_TF_14`)
|no extra answer |safety |no request is answered twice: a one-bit credit per accepted request
(`REQ_TF_15b`)
|request eventually accepted |liveness |every presented request is accepted (`REQ_TF_15a`)
|request eventually answered |liveness |every accepted request is answered (`REQ_TF_15b`)
|===

*Cases:* _two outstanding_, two requests outstanding; _meta FIFO full_, a meta answer arriving
while the FIFO is full; _host answer held_, a host answer held for many cycles while meta answers
arrive; _deadlock precondition_, a TBRE request at the RMW filter while the core's meta answer
waits for its host answer (the deadlock precondition of the design architecture, section "Why meta
answers are always accepted").

*Never:* a meta answer refused; an answer with no request; a request never accepted, or never
answered.

*Run:* _meta answer taken_ and _no extra answer_ in V1; _request eventually accepted_ and _request
eventually answered_ in the liveness run, in checker 1's task where every request is answered
(`task_TagPath_EveryReqAnswered`), which takes assumption A10 and contracts C1 and C3b as given (TB
architecture, Proof order). _Request eventually answered_ also needs the core to take its answers
on `cored_tl_d`: an answer left waiting holds back the next one. Assumption A10 does not list the
core yet (proposed addition P5).

*Blocked by:* Q12 for `REQ_TF_15b`.

'''

=== WTRC

==== How it works

*Rule:* [ToO] WTRC, "A capability store to the NVM ... is not written: it is turned into a `Get` of
the word it targets, with recomputed command integrity, and succeeds only if the NVM already holds
its data and data integrity. It does no lookup."

.WTRC sequence states from [ToO] WTRC; a request out of sequence raises `fatal_fault`
image::cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan_figures.svg#fig3[WTRC sequence states,align=center,width=780,height=370]

[cols="2,4,4",options="header"]
|===
|State |Meaning |Out of sequence here

|`CapIdle` |no capability open |a W1
|`CapW0` |W0 taken, waiting for its W1 |anything but the W1 of the same capability
|`CapW1` |W1 taken, neither answered nor turned into a tag write yet |a W1, or any request before W1
is answered
|`CapTagWr` |W1's tag write issued, waiting for its answer |a W1, or a W0 before W1 is answered
|===

* The states are the spec's description of the sequence, used by the testbench model to tell an
  in-sequence request from one out of sequence; they are not RTL state checked directly.
* "A W0 taken always opens a capability, and W1's answer closes it; the next W0 may be taken in the
  cycle W1 is answered."
* W1's tag write goes ahead of any lookup; a request presented in `CapW1` is out of sequence at
  once, because its lookup could reach the meta port before the tag write.

'''

[[tp_wtrc_store]]
==== wtrc_store: a capability store to the NVM reads, never writes

*Requirements:* `REQ_WTRC_01`, `REQ_WTRC_02`, `REQ_WTRC_03`, `REQ_WTRC_05`, `REQ_WTRC_13`.

*Rule:* for an `NvmCapStore` word `r`: `cored_tl_h` carries a `Get` of `r`{empty}'s word with a
valid command integrity; W0 makes no meta request and W1 none but its tag write; each word is
answered once, `AccessAck`, untagged, `d_source = a_source`, valid response integrity. Every other
access passes unchanged (checked by the `REQ_TF_*` testpoints, run with the WTRC in place).

*Observed at:* `cored_tl_d`, `cored_tl_h`, the meta port.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|sent as a full-word Get |forward |a capability store word presented and not yet forwarded is
presented on `cored_tl_h` as a full-word `Get` of the word it targets, never as a write
(`REQ_WTRC_01`)
|Get has valid command integrity |forward |that `Get` has a valid command integrity
(`REQ_WTRC_02`)
|no lookup for a capability store |backward |no meta request is presented for a capability store
word, except W1's tag write (`REQ_WTRC_03`)
|untagged AccessAck answer |forward |each word's answer is `AccessAck`, untagged, with `d_source`
equal to its `a_source` and a valid response integrity (`REQ_WTRC_05`); that it is answered once is
the `tf_flow` check _no extra answer_
|===

`REQ_WTRC_13`, every other access unchanged and with unchanged timing, has no check of its own: it
follows from the `tf_forward` and `tf_lookup` checks, which run with the WTRC in place.

.Look-alike writes to the NVM and the SRAM
[cols="2,3,1,2,2,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Write |`NvmCapStore` |On `cored_tl_h` |Meta request |Covered by

|capability store W0 to NVM |`csc` W0 to `0x3000_0400`, tag 1, CHERIoT mode |1 |`Get` |none |this testpoint
|capability store W1 to NVM |`csc` W1 to `0x3000_0404`, tag 1, CHERIoT mode |1 |`Get` |the tag write, if matched
|`wtrc_compare`
|word store to NVM |`sw` to `0x3000_0400`, tag 0 |0 |`PutFullData`, unchanged |lookup, tag 0 |`tf_lookup`
|capability store to SRAM |`csc` to `0x1000_1238`, tag 1 |0 |`PutFullData`, unchanged |lookup, tag 1 |`tf_lookup`
|NVM store in ePMP mode |`csc` to `0x3000_0400`, tag 1, ePMP mode |0 |`PutFullData`, unchanged |none |`tf_lookup`
|===

*Edge cases:* _first NVM capability_, `0x3000_0000`, and _last NVM capability_, `0x301F_FFF8`.

*Never:* a write on `cored_tl_h` for a capability store; a lookup for W0; a tagged answer; a broken
response integrity on the WTRC's own answer.

*Run:* V1.

'''

[[tp_wtrc_compare]]
==== wtrc_compare: which stores set the tag

*Requirements:* `REQ_WTRC_04a`, `REQ_WTRC_04b`, `REQ_WTRC_06`, `REQ_WTRC_07`, `REQ_WTRC_08`,
`REQ_WTRC_09`.

*Rule:* `Match(w) = not Faulty(w) and NvmOk(w) and Data(w) == NvmData(w) and
DataIntg(w) == NvmDataIntg(w)`. W0 has `d_error = not Match(W0)`. W1 issues one tag write of tag 1
to `TagWord(c)`, `TagBit(c)` if `Match(W0) and Match(W1)`, after W1's NVM answer and before any
later lookup; W1's `d_error` is the tag write's error if issued, else 1. No mismatch or failed NVM
read raises an alert.

*Precedence:* a word with `Faulty(w)` is decided by <<tp_wtrc_faults>> (`d_error`, no tag write,
alert); this testpoint decides the fault-free words, where a mismatch or a failed NVM read gives
`d_error` and no alert. Witness: a W0 in sequence with only its command integrity broken has
`Faulty`, so `not Match(W0)`: `d_error`, no tag write, and the alert from <<tp_wtrc_faults>>.

*Observed at:* `cored_tl_d`, `cored_tl_h` (the NVM's answers), the meta port, the WTRC's fault
input to the alert.

A tag write is *owed* from the cycle W1's NVM answer arrives, when `Match(W0) and Match(W1)`, until
the meta port takes the tag write.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|W0 error on mismatch |forward, backward |W0's answer has `d_error` exactly when `not Match(W0)`
(`REQ_WTRC_04a`, `REQ_WTRC_04b`)
|only the owed tag write |forward |while a tag write is owed, any meta request presented is that
tag write: a write of
tag 1 to `TagWord(c)`, bit `TagBit(c)` (`REQ_WTRC_06`). With the `tf_lookup` check _no unneeded
lookup_, nothing else reaches the meta port first, and no tag write goes out when none is
owed
|W1 answered after tag write |forward |W1 is answered only after the tag write's answer, with its
`d_error` (`REQ_WTRC_06`, `REQ_WTRC_07`)
|W1 error on mismatch |forward |when W0 or W1 did not match, W1's answer has `d_error` and no tag
write is owed (`REQ_WTRC_08`)
|no alert without a cause |backward |the WTRC's fault input rises only after a cause of
`wtrc_faults` has occurred since reset: a mismatch or a failed NVM read alone raises no alert
(`REQ_WTRC_09`). Since reset, because the alert, once raised, stays raised until reset
(`REQ_TAG_10`)
|answer after NVM answer |backward |each word, W0 or W1, is answered only once its NVM answer has
arrived, now or before: its `d_error` needs `Match(w)`, and `Match(w)` needs that answer
(`REQ_WTRC_04a`, `REQ_WTRC_04b`, `REQ_WTRC_08`)
|===

.Truth table: one cover per row
[cols="2,1,1,1,1,2,1",options="header"]
|===
|Case |`Match(W0)` |`Match(W1)` |Tag write error |W0 `d_error` |Tag write |W1 `d_error`

|both match, tag write ok |1 |1 |0 |0 |yes, tag 1 |0
|both match, tag write error |1 |1 |1 |0 |yes, tag 1 |1
|W1 mismatch |1 |0 |- |0 |none |1
|W0 mismatch |0 |1 |- |1 |none |1
|both mismatch |0 |0 |- |1 |none |1
|===

.Cases: one cause of a mismatch at a time, each covered for W0 and for W1
[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Cause

|NVM read error |the NVM read answers with `d_error`
|data differ in bit 0 |the data differ from the NVM's in bit 0
|data differ in bit 31 |the data differ from the NVM's in bit 31
|only integrity differs |the data equal the NVM's, the data integrity differs
|===

*Edge cases:* _last NVM tag write_, the tag write of the last NVM capability, `0x301F_FFF8`: word
`0x1100_8BFC`, bit 31; _W0 in W1's answer cycle_, a W0 presented in the cycle the previous
capability's W1 is answered.

*Never:* a tag write after a mismatch; a tag write before W1's NVM answer, or behind a later
lookup; a word answered before its NVM answer; an alert for a mismatch or a failed NVM read
(`REQ_WTRC_09`).

*Run:* V1.

*Blocked by:* Q2 for the tag write's bit.

'''

[[tp_wtrc_faults]]
==== wtrc_faults: what the core cannot produce

*Requirements:* `REQ_WTRC_10`, `REQ_WTRC_11`, `REQ_WTRC_12`.

*Rule:* a capability store word out of sequence, partial, with a bad command or data integrity, or
with a bad NVM response integrity is answered with `d_error`, writes no tag and raises
`fatal_fault`; any other request out of sequence raises `fatal_fault`.

*Precedence:* this testpoint decides every word with `Faulty(w)`; <<tp_wtrc_compare>> decides the
rest, and its `Match(w)` includes `not Faulty(w)`, so the two never answer differently.

*Observed at:* `cored_tl_d`, the meta port, the alert sender's request input.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|faulty word answered with error |forward |a capability store word out of sequence, partial, with a
bad command or data integrity, or whose NVM answer has a bad response integrity, is answered with
`d_error`, and no tag write is owed for its capability (`REQ_WTRC_10`)
|faulty word raises alert |liveness |such a word raises the alert request (`REQ_WTRC_11`)
|===

The spec gives no time from the fault to the alert, so _faulty word raises alert_ checks that the
alert request follows,
with no bound. It needs no fairness: nothing outside the design holds it back.

Only the integrity faults can be reached. A word out of sequence or partial needs a core that
breaks its access order (assumptions A3, A4) or sends a tagged partial write (assumption A5), and a
core that does is out of scope (not covered), so _faulty word answered with error_ and _faulty
word raises alert_ are reached through the integrity fault cases below.

.Cases: the integrity faults
[cols="2,2,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |State |Request |Result

|bad data integrity |`CapW0` |W1 with a bad data integrity |`d_error`, no tag, alert
|bad command integrity |`CapIdle` |W0 with a bad command integrity |`d_error`, alert
|bad NVM response integrity |`CapW0` |W0's NVM answer with a bad response integrity |`d_error`, alert
|===

*Edge cases:* _W0 in W1's answer cycle_, a W0 presented in the cycle W1 is answered, is in
sequence: no alert.

*Never:* an alert for a request in sequence and free of integrity faults (`not Faulty`); a tag
write for any of these stores.

*Run:* V1: integrity is free on every port.

*Blocked by:* finding R16. The RTL answers a store with a broken command or NVM response
integrity without `d_error` and lets W1 write the tag; the spec contradicts itself (design
architecture). The expected values above follow the explicit error-handling row and stay
until the designers decide; the three integrity cases fail until then.

The check (former A3) was `REQ_WTRC_12`: any other request out of sequence raises the alert request.
The cases (former cases 1-9) were the sequence table's rows for a request out of sequence (a W1
alone, a second W0, a load or another capability's W1 between W0 and W1, a request during the tag
write) and a tagged `PutPartialData` to the NVM. They needed run V2, which let the core break
assumptions A3, A4 and A5; a core that does is out of scope since (not covered).

'''

[[arb_tps]]
=== 2:1 tag arbiter

==== How it works

*Rule:* [ToO] RMW Filter, "a `cheriot_socket_m1` arbitrates their meta ports, carrying the tag and
bit select sideband, onto the single RMW filter". Input 0 is the core's tag filter, input 1 the
engine's.

* One request passes at a time, with its own tag and bit select; `a_source` grows by one bit, the
  input number. The answer is routed back by that bit, which is then shifted off.
* The tag clear squash between the arbiter and the RMW filter may change only the engine's stale
  clears; core requests pass it unchanged.
* Worked example (both inputs at once) and failure table: design architecture, section "2:1 tag
  arbiter".

'''

[[tp_arb_forward]]
==== arb_forward: each request forwarded once, with its own sideband

*Requirements:* `REQ_ARB_01`, `REQ_ARB_02`, `REQ_ARB_03`, `REQ_ARB_04`, `REQ_ARB_11`.

*Rule:* a request accepted on input `i` leaves the arbiter once, with its A-channel fields, its tag
and its bit select unchanged and `a_source' = (a_source << 1) | i`; a request from input 0 reaches
the RMW filter exactly as the arbiter forwards it.

*Observed at:* the arbiter's three ports; the RMW filter's upstream port for `REQ_ARB_11`.

`Fwd(r, i)` is request `r` as it leaves the arbiter from input `i`: every A-channel field but
`a_source` unchanged, `a_source' = (a_source << 1) | i` kept to 8 bits, the same tag and bit select.
"In the same cycle" is [ToO] Timing: "a request propagates combinationally ... through ... the
`cheriot_socket_m1`{empty}".

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|keeps its own sideband |forward |a request accepted on input `i` leaves the arbiter in the same
cycle, as `Fwd(r, i)` (`REQ_ARB_01`, `REQ_ARB_03`, `REQ_ARB_04`)
|from the named input |backward |a request leaving the arbiter is `Fwd(r, i)` of the request on
input `i = a_source' & 1`, which is accepted in that cycle: none invented, none forwarded twice
(`REQ_ARB_01`, `REQ_ARB_02`)
|core request unchanged |forward |a request from input 0 reaches the RMW filter exactly as it
leaves the arbiter: every A-channel field, the tag and the bit select (`REQ_ARB_11`)
|===

*Cases:* _input 0 alone_; _input 1 alone_; _both, input 0 wins_ and _both, input 1 wins_, both
inputs at once; _input 1 back to back_, back-to-back requests on input 1; _worked example_, a write
of tag 1 to bit 7 on input 0 and a read of bit 8 on input 1 in one cycle.

*Edge cases:* `a_source` _source 0x00_ on each input, _source 0x7F_ on input 1 and _source 0x1F_ on
input 0: the largest source each input's requester sends (assumption A9 keeps the core's top three
bits free); _bit select 0_ and _bit select 31_.

A request whose `a_source` uses bit 7 loses it, as [TLUL] allows: "hosts may only use the low bits
of the identifier and cannot assume the entire `AIW` bits will be returned intact".

*Never:* a request no input presented; input 1's bit select or tag on input 0's request, or the
reverse; a core request changed between the arbiter and the RMW filter.

*Run:* V1.

'''

[[tp_arb_return]]
==== arb_return: each answer to the input that asked

*Requirements:* `REQ_ARB_05`, `REQ_ARB_06`, `REQ_ARB_07`.

*Rule:* an answer with `d_source = s` goes to input `s & 1` only, with `d_source = s >> 1` and every
other D-channel field and the tag unchanged.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|answer to its input |backward |an answer at input `i` is the RMW filter's answer of that cycle,
with `d_source & 1 == i`: never at the other input, never at both (`REQ_ARB_05`)
|source shifted back |forward |that answer carries `d_source = s >> 1` (`REQ_ARB_06`)
|fields unchanged |forward |every other D-channel field and the tag are unchanged (`REQ_ARB_07`)
|taken with its input |forward, backward |the RMW filter's answer is taken in the cycle its input
takes it, and only then: none lost (`REQ_ARB_05`)
|===

With `arb_forward` _keeps its own sideband_ and the TL-UL rule that a device returns `a_source` as
`d_source` ([TLUL]), _source shifted back_ returns to each requester the `a_source` it sent, for
every `a_source` whose bit 7 is 0. No assumption on the engine's `a_source` is needed.

*Cases:* _answer to input 0_ and _answer to input 1_; _alternating inputs_, answers to alternating
inputs in consecutive cycles; _source 0x02 to input 0_, `0x02` goes to input 0 as `0x01`; _source
0x03 to input 1_, `0x03` to input 1 as `0x01`.

*Never:* an answer at both inputs, or at the input that did not ask.

*Run:* V1.

'''

[[tp_arb_flow]]
==== arb_flow: no added cycle, no starvation

*Requirements:* `REQ_ARB_08`, `REQ_ARB_09`, `REQ_ARB_10`.

*Rule:* a request alone reaches the RMW filter in the cycle it is presented, and an answer reaches
its input in the cycle the RMW filter gives it; a request held on either input is eventually
accepted, given the RMW filter keeps accepting.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|alone in same cycle |forward |a request presented on input `i` while the other input presents
none is presented to the RMW filter in the same cycle, as `Fwd(r, i)` (`REQ_ARB_09`)
|answer at once |forward |the RMW filter's answer with `d_source = s` is presented at input
`s & 1` in the same cycle (`REQ_ARB_10`)
|no starvation |liveness |a request held on either input is eventually accepted, given the RMW
filter keeps accepting (`REQ_ARB_08`)
|===

*Cases:* _input 0 alone_; _input 1 alone_; _starvation case_, input 1 presenting in every cycle
while input 0 waits (input 0 must still be accepted).

*Never:* a cycle added on the way out or back; an input starved.

*Run:* the latency checks in V1; `REQ_ARB_08` in the liveness run (checker 1's
`task_TagPath_EveryReqAnswered`), or in a bounded safety form once Q15 names the policy.

*Blocked by:* Q15 (arbitration policy) for `REQ_ARB_08`.

'''

[[rmw_tps]]
=== RMW filter

==== How it works

*Rule:* [ToO] RMW Filter, "A read is forwarded and the tag bit is picked out of the response word. A
write is turned into a `Get` of the meta word"; the word is written back only when the bit must
change.

* `Bit(W, b) = (W >> b) & 1` is the tag in word `W` at bit select `b`.
* `Upd(W, b, t) = (W & ~(1 << b)) | (t << b)` is the word written back: bit `b` set to `t`, every
  other bit kept.
* One operation at a time; a new request is taken only when nothing is unanswered, or in the cycle a
  read is answered.
* An *operation* is a request accepted on the upstream port, until its answer is taken there.
  Its downstream requests are its `Get` and, for a write whose bit changes, its write-back.
* The `Get` may be presented downstream while its request is still presented upstream and not yet
  accepted: the request passes combinationally ([ToO] Timing). The checks allow that, and require
  the upstream request to be accepted in the cycle the `Get` is.
* A *faulty `Get` answer* is the `Get` answer of a write with no `d_error` and a broken response or
  data integrity. [ToO] Error Handling raises `fatal_fault` for it and says nothing more, and the
  alert stays raised until reset, so the testplan claims nothing about what the filter does for that
  write after the answer: whether it writes back and how often, what it writes (its `a_source` too)
  and how the write is answered (its `d_error` too) (checker 1 uarch). Still claimed:
  its `Get` with its `a_source`, one answer per operation, and the alert (`tag_alerts`).
* The four states and worked examples: design architecture, section "RMW filter".

'''

[[tp_rmw_read]]
==== rmw_read: a read returns its bit

*Requirements:* `REQ_RMW_01`, `REQ_RMW_02`, `REQ_RMW_11`, `REQ_RMW_18` (the `Get` of a write too).

*Rule:* a read issues one `Get` of its meta word downstream; its answer's tag is `Bit(W, b)` (not
checked with `d_error`); a read presented in the cycle the previous read is answered is accepted
then, if the downstream port is ready.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|Get carries valid integrity |forward |every Get presented on the port carries a valid command integrity (`REQ_RMW_18`; nothing else checks it: the TL-UL ABVIP leaves every integrity field free)
|Get of its meta word |forward |a read's downstream request is a `Get` of its meta word, with its
`a_source` (`REQ_RMW_01`)
|returns its tag bit |forward |a read's answer without `d_error` has the tag `Bit(W, b)`, with `W`
the word of its `Get` answer (`REQ_RMW_02`)
|back-to-back read accepted |forward |a read presented in the cycle the previous read is answered,
with the downstream port ready, is accepted in that cycle (`REQ_RMW_11`)
|===

*Cases:* the word read, _word all zeros_ `0x0000_0000`, _word all ones_ `0xFFFF_FFFF`, _word AAAA_
`0xAAAA_AAAA`, _word 5555_ `0x5555_5555` and _word with one bit_, a single bit at `b`; the bit
select, _bit select 0_, _bit select 7_, _bit select 31_; _reads back to back_, reads in consecutive
cycles.

*Never:* a read turned into a write; the tag of another bit.

*Run:* V1.

'''

[[tp_rmw_write_skip]]
==== rmw_write_skip: an equal bit is not written

*Requirements:* `REQ_RMW_03`, `REQ_RMW_04`, `REQ_RMW_05`.

*Rule:* a write first issues a full-word `Get` of its meta word; if `Bit(W, b) == t` it issues no
write-back and is answered `AccessAck`. A write is answered only once its `Get`{empty}'s answer has
arrived: [ToO] RMW Filter, `Fill`, "the read response is converted into an `AccessAck`{empty}".

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|full-word Get first |forward |a write's first downstream request is a full-word `Get` of its meta
word (`REQ_RMW_03`)
|no write-back |backward |no write-back is presented for a write whose `Get` answer has its bit
equal to the tag (`REQ_RMW_04`)
|answered with AccessAck |forward |such a write is answered with `AccessAck` (`REQ_RMW_05`)
|answer after Get answer |backward |a write is answered only once its `Get`{empty}'s answer has
arrived, now or before (`REQ_RMW_03`, `REQ_RMW_05`; for a write-back, `rmw_write_back` _write-back
answer passed up_)
|===

_No write-back_ and _answered with AccessAck_ claim nothing when the write's `Get` answer is faulty
(<<rmw_tps>>, How it works).

.Truth table: stored bit and tag to write
[cols="2,1,1,2,3",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Stored bit |Tag |Write-back |Testpoint

|bit and tag 0 |0 |0 |no |this one
|bit and tag 1 |1 |1 |no |this one
|- |0 |1 |yes |`rmw_write_back` _tag 1 over stored 0_
|- |1 |0 |yes |`rmw_write_back` _tag 0 over stored 1_
|===

*Cases:* the write's requester, for _full-word Get first_: _core write's Get_, the core's tag filter
(arbiter input 0); _engine write's Get_, the engine's tag filter (arbiter input 1); each sending its
`Get`.

*Never:* a write-back when the bit is equal; a write with no `Get` first; a write answered before
its `Get`{empty}'s answer.

*Run:* V1.

'''

[[tp_rmw_write_back]]
==== rmw_write_back: a changed bit is written back alone

*Requirements:* `REQ_RMW_06`, `REQ_RMW_07`, `REQ_RMW_08`, `REQ_RMW_09`.

*Rule:* if `Bit(W, b) != t`, the filter writes back `Upd(W, b, t)` with one full-word `PutFullData`
to the same meta word, with freshly computed command and data integrity; the write-back's answer is
forwarded as the write's answer; every downstream request of the write carries its `a_source`.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|carries the updated word |forward |the write-back of a write whose bit differs carries the word
`Upd(W, b, t)` (`REQ_RMW_06`)
|full-word Put to same word |forward |it is a full-word `PutFullData` to the same meta word, with a
valid command and data integrity (`REQ_RMW_07`)
|write-back answer passed up |forward |such a write is answered only with its write-back's answer,
in the same cycle, carrying its `d_opcode` and `d_error` (`REQ_RMW_08`)
|keeps the write's source |forward |every downstream request of a write carries the write's
`a_source` (`REQ_RMW_09`)
|===

_Carries the updated word_, _full-word Put to same word_ and _write-back answer passed up_, and
_keeps the write's source_ for the write-back, claim nothing when the write's `Get` answer is faulty
(<<rmw_tps>>, How it works).

.Cases
[cols="2,2,2,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Word read |Write |Word written back

|clear bit 7 |`0x0000_0080` |tag 0 to bit 7 |`0x0000_0000`
|set bit 8 |`0x0000_0080` |tag 1 to bit 8 |`0x0000_0180`
|clear bit 31 |`0xFFFF_FFFF` |tag 0 to bit 31 |`0x7FFF_FFFF`
|set bit 0 |`0x0000_0000` |tag 1 to bit 0 |`0x0000_0001`
|set bit in word AAAA |`0xAAAA_AAAA` |tag 1 to bit 0 |`0xAAAA_AAAB`
|===

_Tag 1 over stored 0_ and _tag 0 over stored 1_ are the last two rows of the `rmw_write_skip` truth
table: stored bit 0 with tag 1, and stored bit 1 with tag 0.

*Never:* any other bit changed; a write-back to another word; a stale integrity; a second
write-back.

*Run:* V1.

'''

[[tp_rmw_single_op]]
==== rmw_single_op: one operation at a time

*Requirements:* `REQ_RMW_10`, `REQ_RMW_15`, `REQ_RMW_16`.

*Rule:* a new request is accepted only when no operation is unanswered, or in the cycle the only
unanswered operation, a read, is answered; every accepted request is answered once, given the meta
SRAM answers; the downstream port carries one `Get` per accepted request, plus one write-back for a
write whose bit changes, and nothing else.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|one operation at a time |backward |a request is accepted only when no operation is unanswered, or
in the cycle the only unanswered operation, a read, is answered (`REQ_RMW_10`)
|nothing else downstream |backward |every downstream request is the `Get` of the current or the
presented request, or the write-back of the current write whose bit differs, each once; a `Get`
taken for a presented request is accepted upstream in that cycle (`REQ_RMW_16`)
|one answer per operation |backward |an answer is presented upstream only while an operation is
unanswered: one answer per operation (`REQ_RMW_15`)
|every operation answered |liveness |every accepted request is answered, given the meta SRAM
answers (`REQ_RMW_15`)
|===

The write-back slot of _nothing else downstream_ is also open for a write whose `Get` answer is
faulty, whether or not its bit
differs, until the write is answered: what the filter sends there is not claimed (<<rmw_tps>>, How
it works).

*Cases:* _write then read_, a write followed by a read (the read waits for the write-back's
answer); _reads back to back_; _write then write_, a write followed by a write; _filters
interleaved_, requests from both tag filters interleaved.

*Never:* two operations in flight; a write-back for a read; a request downstream with no request
upstream.

*Run:* _one operation at a time_, _nothing else downstream_ and _one answer per operation_ in V1;
_every operation answered_ in the liveness run with contract C1 (checker 1's
`task_TagPath_EveryReqAnswered`).

'''

[[tp_rmw_errors]]
==== rmw_errors: device errors

*Requirements:* `REQ_RMW_13`, `REQ_RMW_14`, `REQ_RMW_17`.

*Rule:* a device error on the `Get` of a write aborts it: no write-back; a device error on any meta
SRAM answer reaches the requester as `d_error`, and only such an answer does. The alert is
`tag_alerts`.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|Get error stops the write |backward |no write-back is presented for a write whose `Get` answer has
`d_error` (`REQ_RMW_13`)
|error passed up |forward |an operation whose downstream answer has `d_error` is answered upstream
with `d_error` (`REQ_RMW_14`)
|no error without a cause |backward |an answer upstream has `d_error` only when its operation's
`Get` answer or write-back answer has `d_error` (`REQ_RMW_17`)
|===

_Error passed up_ and _no error without a cause_ claim nothing for a write whose `Get` answer is
faulty, even when its write-back is
answered with `d_error` (<<rmw_tps>>, How it works).

*Cases:* `d_error` on a read's answer, _read answer error_; on a write's `Get`, with the bit equal,
_Get error, bit equal_, and with it different, _Get error, bit differs_; on a write-back's answer,
_write-back error_. These reach the precondition of _no error without a cause_; the answers it keeps
free of an error are those of `rmw_read`, `rmw_write_skip` and `rmw_write_back`.

*Never:* a write-back after an errored `Get`; an error answer passed up without `d_error`; an error
answer upstream with no error downstream.

*Run:* V1.

[[checker2]]
== Checker 2: meta access

Checker 2 holds the four access checkers and the 4:1 arbiter, from the four requester ports to
`meta_sram_tl` (xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#meta_access[TB architecture, checker
2]). Every requester and the meta SRAM's answers are driven by the testbench; the requests are free,
so illegal ones are the point.

=== Access checkers and 4:1 arbiter

==== How it works

*Rule:* [ToO] Access Checkers, "An access is forwarded only if all of the following hold: ...
Everything else is steered to a `tlul_err_resp` instance and answered with a TL-UL error."; [ToO]
Arbitration, "A `tlul_socket_m1` arbitrates the four checked streams onto `meta_sram_tl`."

[cols="1,2,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|Input |Requester port |Region it owns |Who uses it

|0 |`corerevbm_tl` |`0x1100_0000`-`0x1100_0BFF`: the revocation bitmap |the core's TRVK filter
|1 |tag port |`0x1100_0C00`-`0x1100_97FF`: NVM tags, then main SRAM tags |the RMW filter, for both
tag filters
|2 |`revbm_tl_d` |the revocation bitmap |software, through `xbar_main`
|3 |the engine's bitmap port |the revocation bitmap |the engine's TRVK filter
|===

* A request is forwarded only if `Legal(p, r)`; otherwise it is answered with a TL-UL error and never
  reaches the meta SRAM.
* The 4:1 arbiter takes the *checked streams*, the access checkers' outputs and its own host ports
  ([ToO] Arbitration: "the four checked streams"), in round-robin order and adds two `a_source`
  bits, the input number, which route the answer back.
* Requests and answers pass in the cycle they are presented ([ToO] Timing: zero-depth FIFOs).
* *Input* numbers each port by the 4:1 arbiter input it is wired to; port `i` in a cover formula is
  that number. Which port sits on which input is wiring: no expected value depends on it, since
  each check uses its own port's number.

'''

[[tp_meta_forward]]
==== meta_forward: a legal request reaches the meta SRAM once, unchanged

*Requirements:* `REQ_META_01`, `REQ_META_02`, `REQ_META_08`, `REQ_META_14`.

*Rule:* a request with `Legal(p, r)` is forwarded to `meta_sram_tl` exactly once, with every
A-channel field unchanged except `a_source = (a_source << 2) | i`, `i` the port's input of the 4:1
arbiter; alone, it reaches `meta_sram_tl` in the cycle it is presented; `meta_sram_tl` carries
nothing else.

*Observed at:* the four requester ports and `meta_sram_tl`.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|legal request forwarded |forward |a legal request appears on `meta_sram_tl` with its fields
(`REQ_META_01`, `REQ_META_02`), in the same cycle when no other port presents one (`REQ_META_14`)
|no extra meta SRAM request |backward |every request on `meta_sram_tl` belongs to one legal request
presented on a port and not yet forwarded: none invented (`REQ_META_08`), none twice
(`REQ_META_01`)
|===

*Cases:* _legal Get_, a legal `Get` accepted on port `i`, one cover per port; _legal Put_, a legal
`PutFullData` on port `i`, one cover per port; _two ports at once_, _three ports at once_ and _four
ports at once_, two, three and four ports presenting legal requests in one cycle.

*Edge cases:* _region first word_ and _region last word_, the first and last word of port
`i`{empty}'s region, one cover each per port: `0x1100_0000` and `0x1100_0BFC` on the bitmap ports
(0, 2, 3), `0x1100_0C00` and `0x1100_97FC` on the tag port (1).

*Never:* a request on `meta_sram_tl` that no port presented; a forwarded request with a changed
address, opcode, size, mask, data or integrity.

*Run:* V1.

*Blocked by:* open decision D28 of the
xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_meta_access_uarch.adoc#open_decisions[checker 2 uarch]: whether
the same-cycle part of _legal request forwarded_ (`REQ_META_14`) also holds for a legal request presented while a refused
request of its own port is still unanswered.

'''

[[tp_meta_refuse]]
==== meta_refuse: an illegal request is answered with an error, never forwarded

*Requirements:* `REQ_META_03`, `REQ_META_04`, `REQ_META_05`, `REQ_META_06`, `REQ_META_07`,
`REQ_META_16`.

*Rule:* a request with `not Legal(p, r)` never reaches `meta_sram_tl` and is answered exactly once,
with `d_error` and a valid response integrity.

*Observed at:* the four requester ports and `meta_sram_tl`.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|in own region |backward |every request on `meta_sram_tl` lies in the region of the port it came
from, the port `a_source & 3` names (`REQ_META_03`)
|only in CHERIoT mode |backward |every request on `meta_sram_tl` comes in CHERIoT mode, `Ena`
(`REQ_META_04`)
|only full words |backward |every request on `meta_sram_tl` is a full word, `FullWord(r)`
(`REQ_META_05`)
|only Get or PutFullData |backward |every request on `meta_sram_tl` is a `Get` or a `PutFullData`
(`REQ_META_06`)
|illegal request gets error |forward |the answer to a request that is not legal carries `d_error`
(`REQ_META_07`). It comes at most once by the TL-UL protocol check, as an answer names an
outstanding request (`tlul_protocol` _TL-UL rules hold_), and at least once by the
every-request-answered check (`meta_flow` _request eventually answered_)
|error answer carries valid integrity |forward |the answer to a request that is not legal carries
a valid response integrity and, for a `Get`, a valid data integrity (`REQ_META_16`): a denial
software can cause must not become an integrity fault at the requester
|===

.Truth table: the four conditions, one cover per row and per port (64 covers)
[cols="1,1,1,1,2",options="header"]
|===
|`Ena` |In region |Full word |`Get` or `PutFullData` |Result

|1 |1 |1 |1 |forwarded (`meta_forward`)
|any other combination (15 rows) | | | |refused: `d_error`, not forwarded
|===

The _truth table row_ covers: one per row `r` and port `i`, with `r` read from the four columns as
bits, `Ena` the most significant: row 15 is the forwarded one.

.Cases: one condition broken from a legal request
[cols="2,1,4",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Broken |Request

|ePMP mode |mode |`cheriot_ena_i` = `MuBi4False`
|invalid mode |mode |an invalid `cheriot_ena_i` value such as `4'h0`
|tag port reads bitmap |region |tag port reads `0x1100_0100` (the bitmap)
|software reads tag word |region |`revbm_tl_d` reads `0x1100_8C48` (a tag word)
|outside the meta SRAM |region |any port, `0x1100_9800` (the meta SRAM top) and `0x10FF_FFFC`
(below the base)
|sub-word Get |size |a `Get` of one byte (`a_size` = 0) and of two bytes (`a_size` = 1)
|partial Put |opcode |a `PutPartialData` of all four bytes
|===

*Edge cases:* _bitmap last word_ and _tag first word_, the region seam seen from each port `i`, one
cover each per port: a full-word `Get` of `0x1100_0BFC`, legal on the bitmap ports and illegal on
the tag port; of `0x1100_0C00`, the reverse. _Late answer_, one cover per port: a refused request
on port `i` answered a cycle or more after it was taken: _illegal request gets error_ seen on an
answer that waited.

*Never:* an illegal request on `meta_sram_tl`; an illegal request with no answer or two; an
illegal request answered without `d_error`.

*Run:* V1. TL-UL host rules (assumption A8) already exclude a word-unaligned full-word access
(`addrSizeAligned`) and undefined opcodes, so a request refused only for its alignment is
unreachable; the alignment condition is reached through sub-word sizes.

*Note:* `REQ_META_07` asks for one answer with `d_error`. The answer's other fields are checked by
`tlul_protocol` (`d_opcode`, `d_size`, `d_source`); no requirement yet asks for a valid response
integrity on it (proposed addition P1).

'''

[[tp_meta_return]]
==== meta_return: each answer to its own requester, unchanged

*Requirements:* `REQ_META_09`, `REQ_META_10`, `REQ_META_11`, `REQ_META_15`.

*Rule:* an answer on `meta_sram_tl` with `d_source = s` goes to input `s & 3` only, with
`d_source = s >> 2` and every other D-channel field unchanged, in the cycle it arrives.

*Observed at:* the four requester ports and `meta_sram_tl`.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|answer to its port |forward |an answer on `meta_sram_tl` with `d_source = s` is presented at port
`s & 3` in the same cycle (`REQ_META_09`, `REQ_META_15`)
|source shifted back |forward |with `d_source = s >> 2` (`REQ_META_10`)
|fields unchanged |forward |with every other D-channel field unchanged; `d_data` only in an
`AccessAckData`, the one answer that carries data ([TLUL]) (`REQ_META_11`)
|taken with its port |forward |the meta SRAM's answer is taken exactly when its port takes it
(`REQ_META_09`)
|only the meta SRAM's answer |backward |the answer a port gets to a legal request is the meta SRAM's
answer to it, in the same cycle: no port gets an answer the meta SRAM did not send it
(`REQ_META_09`)
|===

*Cases:* _answer to each port_, an answer to port `i`, one cover per port; _ports back to back_,
answers in consecutive cycles to different ports; _worked example_, `0x56` returns to port 2 as
`0x15`; _late answer_, one cover per port: a legal request on port `i` answered a cycle or more
after it was taken: _only the meta SRAM's answer_ seen on an answer that waited.

*Edge cases:* _source top bits_, a returned `d_source` of `0x3F`, every bit a port may use
(assumption A9: the top two bits stay free); _error answer_, an answer with `d_error`; _bad response
integrity_, an answer with a broken response integrity. Both pass unchanged.

*Never:* an answer at the wrong port or at two ports; a changed `d_data`, `d_error` or integrity.

*Run:* V1.

'''

[[tp_meta_flow]]
==== meta_flow: round robin, every request answered

*Requirements:* `REQ_META_12`, `REQ_META_13`.

*Rule:* round robin ([TLUL] `tlul_socket_m1`: "Requests coming from each host ports are arbitrated
in the socket based on round-robin scheme"): while a request waits at a host port of the 4:1
arbiter, a checked stream, at most three requests of the other host ports are forwarded before it.
A request presented on a requester port is accepted unless the requester withdraws or changes it
first, and every accepted request is answered exactly once, given the meta SRAM accepts and answers
and the requesters take their answers. A changed request is a new one: TileLink guarantees
acceptance only for "presented beats", held unchanged "until ready is also HIGH" ([TL] §5.1, p29).

*Observed at:* the 4:1 arbiter's four host ports and `meta_sram_tl` for _round robin bound_; the
four requester ports for the other checks.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|round robin bound |safety |the bounded form of round robin, at the arbiter's host ports: at most
three grants to the other inputs while a request waits. It implies `REQ_META_12` at the arbiter when
the meta SRAM keeps accepting, and needs no fairness assumption
|no extra answer |safety |no request answered twice: an answer only to an outstanding request
(`tlul_protocol` _TL-UL rules hold_ on each requester port)
|request eventually answered |liveness |every accepted request is answered (`REQ_META_13`)
|request eventually accepted |liveness |a request presented on a requester port is accepted, unless
the requester withdraws or changes it first (`REQ_META_12` at the port)
|===

*Cases:* _all four present_, all four host ports of the arbiter presenting in one cycle; _waits for
three_, one cover per input `i`: input `i` waits while the other three are granted, one each, then
is granted itself.

*Never:* a request at a host port of the arbiter passed over by a fourth grant to the others; an
accepted request answered twice, or never; a request held on a requester port never accepted while
the meta SRAM accepts and answers and the requester takes its answers.

*Run:* _round robin bound_ and _no extra answer_ in V1. _Request eventually accepted_ in liveness
A, which assumes only `REQ_META_12`{empty}'s own condition, that the meta SRAM keeps accepting;
_request eventually answered_ in liveness B (assumptions A10 and A16, contracts C4, C5; checker 2
uarch D35). run variants names the Jasper task of each.

*Blocked by:* open decision D28 of the
xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_meta_access_uarch.adoc#open_decisions[checker 2 uarch], for
`REQ_META_12`{empty}'s condition: a legal request waits while a refused request of its own port is
unanswered, so the requester must also take its answers.

'''

[[tp_tag_isolation]]
==== tag_isolation: the tag store is reached only by the tag path

*Requirements:* `REQ_TAG_05`, `REQ_TAG_06`, `REQ_TAG_11`.

*Rule:* a request from the tag port reaches `meta_sram_tl` only inside `0x1100_0C00`-`0x1100_97FF`
and only when `Ena`; a request from the other three ports never reaches that range. These are the
tag path's part of `REQ_META_03` and `REQ_META_04`, kept as their own requirements because they
carry the countermeasure `MEM.SW_NOACCESS` ("The capability tag store is not memory mapped").

*Observed at:* `meta_sram_tl`; the requester ports for the covers.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|tag port in tag regions |backward |a request on `meta_sram_tl` from the tag port lies in
`0x1100_0C00`-`0x1100_97FF` (`REQ_TAG_05`)
|tag port only in CHERIoT mode |backward |a request on `meta_sram_tl` from the tag port comes only
in CHERIoT mode (`REQ_TAG_06`)
|other ports never reach tags |backward |a request on `meta_sram_tl` from any other port lies
outside `0x1100_0C00`-`0x1100_97FF` (`REQ_TAG_11`)
|===

*Cases:* _every mode value_, a request taken on the tag port in each of the 16 `cheriot_ena_i`
values, one cover per value; _software at first tag word_, _software at middle tag word_ and
_software at last tag word_, `revbm_tl_d` at `0x1100_0C00`, `0x1100_8C48`, `0x1100_97FC`; _core
TRVK at tag word_, `corerevbm_tl` at `0x1100_0C00`; _engine at tag word_, the engine's bitmap port
at `0x1100_0C00`.

*Never:* a tag-region address on `meta_sram_tl` that came from a bitmap port; any tag port request
on `meta_sram_tl` in ePMP mode; a tag port request on `meta_sram_tl` outside the tag regions.

*Run:* V1.

[[checker3]]
== Checker 3: revocation engine

Checker 3 holds the engine (mover, TRVK filter, socket, tag filter), its sweep control, the
interrupt, the core write watch, the tag clear squash and the 2:1 tag arbiter
(xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#revocation_checker[TB architecture, checker 3]). The
register file is a blackbox there: its outputs to the engine follow the register file model,
contract C20, and the checks look at what the engine writes into the register file, not at
`regs_tl_d`. The register behaviour itself is checked by the CSR testing (<<tp_csr>>). The testbench
drives the register file's outputs (software's writes), the core's writes, the answers on
`tbre_tl_h` (any capability data), the bitmap answers and the RMW filter's answers. The engine's
terms (taken start, swept capabilities, revoked, watch window, touch) are defined in <<defs_sweep>>
and <<defs_capability>>; how each check is performed is in the
xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_revocation_uarch.adoc[checker 3 uarch].

=== Start, status and interrupt

==== How it works

*Rule:* [ToO] Revocation Engine, "While the engine is active, from the cycle after a taken start
until every capability of the sweep is resolved, `TBRE_REGWEN` is low and locks the three
registers; `TBRE_STATUS.busy` follows one cycle later. ... When the engine stops being active, the
