`tbre_done` interrupt is raised."

[cols="1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Cycle |What happens

|1 |Software writes 1 to `TBRE_START`; `TBRE_REGWEN` is 1, CHERIoT mode, `NUM` = 1, `BASE` in the
main SRAM: a taken start.
|2 |`TBRE_REGWEN` falls and `TBRE_EPOCH` turns odd (4 to 5) in the same cycle: the engine is active.
The engine presents the read of W0.
|3 |`TBRE_STATUS.busy` rises, one cycle after `TBRE_REGWEN` fell. The read of W1 is presented.
|4-7 |The reads are answered; the bitmap lookup and the clear, if any, are made and answered.
|8 |The capability is resolved: `TBRE_REGWEN` rises, `TBRE_EPOCH` goes from 5 to 6 (no error was seen), the engine stops being active.
|9 |`INTR_STATE.tbre_done` is set; `TBRE_STATUS.busy` falls, one cycle after `TBRE_REGWEN` rose.
|11 |Software writes 1 to `TBRE_START` with `NUM` = 0: an ignored start.
|12 |`TBRE_STATUS.start_err` is set; `TBRE_REGWEN`, `busy` and `TBRE_EPOCH` do not move.
|===

The cycles of the reads, the answers and the interrupt are one example; the tool tries every
timing. The relations the spec fixes are exact: `TBRE_REGWEN` falls in the cycle after the start,
`TBRE_EPOCH.active` is its inverse in the same cycle, `busy` follows one cycle later.

With the register file a blackbox, "software writes 1 to ``TBRE_START``" is the register file's
write strobe for `TBRE_START`, with the value 1, and `busy`, `start_err` and `sweep_err` are what
the engine writes into `TBRE_STATUS`: a *set request*, the field's write enable with the value 1.
`TBRE_REGWEN` and `TBRE_EPOCH` are `hwext` registers ([HJSON]): software reads what the engine
drives, so the checks read it directly.

'''

[[tp_tbre_start]]
==== tbre_start: which starts start a sweep

*Requirements:* `REQ_TBRE_01`, `REQ_TBRE_02`, `REQ_TBRE_03`, `REQ_TBRE_04a`.

*Rule:* a `TakenStart` starts a sweep over `Swept`; an `IgnoredStart` starts nothing, leaves
`TBRE_STATUS.busy`, `TBRE_REGWEN` and `TBRE_EPOCH` unchanged and sets `start_err`; `start_err` is
set by nothing else. That `start_err` stays set, that locked writes have no effect and that the
registers keep their values (`REQ_TBRE_04b`, `REQ_TBRE_05`, `REQ_TBRE_06`) is register file
behaviour: <<tp_csr>>.

*Observed at:* the register file's outputs (`TBRE_START`, `TBRE_BASE_ADDR`, `TBRE_NUM_CAPS`), the
engine's writes into `TBRE_STATUS`, `TBRE_REGWEN`, `TBRE_EPOCH`.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|taken start activates |forward |a taken start makes the engine active: `TBRE_REGWEN` is 0 in
the next cycle (`REQ_TBRE_01`; the same obligation as `tbre_status` _REGWEN low after start_)
|REGWEN falls only on start |backward |`TBRE_REGWEN` falls only in the cycle after a taken start,
so an ignored start starts no sweep (`REQ_TBRE_01`, `REQ_TBRE_02`)
|ignored start changes nothing |stable |in the cycle after an ignored start, `TBRE_REGWEN` is still
1, `TBRE_EPOCH` is as before and the busy field is 0: the start moves none of them
(`REQ_TBRE_02`). Busy is 0, not "as before": when the start comes in the cycle a sweep ends, busy
falls then, as the busy check (`tbre_status` _busy follows REGWEN_) requires (checker 3 uarch U54)
|ignored start sets error |forward |an ignored start is followed by a `start_err` set request, at
some point (`REQ_TBRE_03`; no bound in the spec, P7)
|error set next cycle |forward |that set request comes no later than the cycle after the ignored
start, so the first register read after the start sees it (`REQ_TBRE_03`; DV reading, gap, raised with the designers)
|error only after ignored start |backward |a `start_err` set request comes only while an ignored
start has not had one yet: a one-bit credit (`REQ_TBRE_04a`)
|===

.Truth table: the three start conditions (`TBRE_REGWEN` = 1, rule R1 of contract C20), one cover per row
[cols="1,1,1,2",options="header"]
|===
|`Ena` |`NUM != 0` |`Tagged(BASE)` |Result

|1 |1 |1 |sweep starts
|1 |1 |0 |ignored, `start_err`
|1 |0 |1 |ignored, `start_err`
|1 |0 |0 |ignored, `start_err`
|0 |1 |1 |ignored, `start_err`
|0 |1 |0 |ignored, `start_err`
|0 |0 |1 |ignored, `start_err`
|0 |0 |0 |ignored, `start_err`
|===

Each row is one cover of the _truth table row_ family: 8 covers.

.Cases: one input varied from a taken start (`BASE` = `0x1000_0000`, `NUM` = 1, CHERIoT mode)
[cols="2,2,3,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Varied |Value |Result

|NVM base |`BASE` |`0x3000_0000` (NVM) |starts
|last SRAM capability |`BASE` |`0x1002_FFF8` (last main SRAM capability) |starts, `N` = 1
|SRAM top |`BASE` |`0x1003_0000` (main SRAM top) |ignored
|below SRAM |`BASE` |`0x0FFF_FFF8` |ignored
|below NVM |`BASE` |`0x2FFF_FFF8` |ignored
|NVM top |`BASE` |`0x3020_0000` (NVM top) |ignored
|meta SRAM base |`BASE` |`0x1100_0000` (meta SRAM) |ignored
|peripheral base |`BASE` |`0x4000_0000` (a peripheral) |ignored
|zero capabilities |`NUM` |0 |ignored
|largest NUM |`NUM` |`0x7FFF_FFFF` |starts; `N` clipped (<<tp_tbre_sweep>>)
|ePMP mode |mode |`MuBi4False` |ignored
|invalid mode |mode |an invalid `cheriot_ena_i`, `4'h0` |ignored
|===

*Edge cases:* _write of 0_, a write of 0 to `TBRE_START`: nothing happens; _same range again_, a
second start after a sweep, with no register write between: the same range is swept again; _error
again_, an ignored start while `start_err` is already set: a set request again.

*Never:* a sweep from an ignored start; a `start_err` set request after a taken start; an ignored
start that moves `TBRE_REGWEN`, busy or the epoch.

*Run:* V1, with the register file blackboxed and its outputs following contract C20.

*Blocked by:* Q42 for _error set next cycle_.

'''

[[tp_tbre_status]]
==== tbre_status: active, busy and the first read

*Requirements:* `REQ_TBRE_07`, `REQ_TBRE_08`, `REQ_TBRE_09`; `REQ_TBRE_12` by composition.

*Rule:* `TBRE_REGWEN` falls in the cycle after a `TakenStart` and stays 0 until every swept
capability is `Resolved`, and is 1 at all other times; `busy(t) = not TBRE_REGWEN(t-1)`;
`TBRE_EPOCH.active(t) = not TBRE_REGWEN(t)`.

*Observed at:* `TBRE_REGWEN`, the engine's writes of `TBRE_STATUS.busy`, `TBRE_EPOCH`; the engine's
ports, for what is still outstanding.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|REGWEN low after start |forward |`TBRE_REGWEN` is 0 in the cycle after a taken start
(`REQ_TBRE_07`)
|REGWEN rises only when resolved |backward |`TBRE_REGWEN` rises only when the tracked capability
of the sweep is resolved and no read, lookup or clear of the engine is outstanding (`REQ_TBRE_07`;
the proposed reading of `Resolved`, gap, raised with the designers)
|busy follows REGWEN |forward |in every cycle, the busy field equals not `TBRE_REGWEN` of the cycle
before; the busy field is what the engine last wrote into it (`REQ_TBRE_08`; its storage is the
register file's, contract C20)
|active follows REGWEN |forward |in every cycle, `TBRE_EPOCH.active` equals not `TBRE_REGWEN`
(`REQ_TBRE_09`)
|===

*`REQ_TBRE_12`* (the first read after a start sees the sweep) follows from _REGWEN low after start_,
_busy follows REGWEN_ and _active follows REGWEN_, which make `TBRE_REGWEN` 0 and the epoch odd from
the cycle after the start and busy 1 a cycle later, and from `REQ_REG_02` (the register interface
takes a request at most every other cycle), which the CSR testing checks (<<tp_csr>>).

*Cases:* _sweep of one_, a sweep of one capability; _two in flight_, of two, with both words in
flight; _last capability cleared_, one whose last capability needs a clear, so the clear's answer
is the last part to arrive; _each tracking phase_, one cover per phase of the tracked capability,
`TrkIdle` to `TrkResolved`; _tracked first_, _tracked in middle_ and _tracked last_, the tracked
capability first in its sweep, in the middle and last; _reset mid sweep_, a reset in the middle of
a sweep.

*Never:* `TBRE_REGWEN` rising while a read, a lookup or a clear of the sweep is outstanding;
`busy` or `active` out of step.

*Run:* V1.

*Blocked by:* Q16 for _REGWEN rises only when resolved_.

'''

[[tp_tbre_epoch]]
==== tbre_epoch: the epoch counts sweeps without an error

*Requirements:* `REQ_TBRE_10`, `REQ_TBRE_11`.

*Rule:* `count(t) = count(t-1) + 1 mod 2^31^` if `active` falls at `t` and no error cause of
<<tp_tbre_errors>> occurred during that sweep, the cycle `active` falls included; otherwise
`count(t) = count(t-1)`.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|steps unless error |forward |in the cycle `TBRE_EPOCH.active` falls, the count is the old count
plus 1 if no error cause occurred in the sweep, else the old count (`REQ_TBRE_10`, `REQ_TBRE_11`)
|count stable otherwise |stable |in every other cycle, the count is unchanged (`REQ_TBRE_11`)
|===

.Cases
[cols="2,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Sweep |`TBRE_EPOCH`

|clean sweep |taken start, no error |4, 5, 6
|read error |taken start, a sweep read answered with `d_error` (no alert) |4, 5, 4
|bitmap error |taken start, a bitmap lookup error (alert) |4, 5, 4
|ignored start |ignored start |4
|ignored after end |an ignored start in the cycle after a sweep ended |6 stays 6
|error left set |`sweep_err` left set by an earlier sweep, this sweep with no error |4, 5, 6:
counted ([ToO]: "A sweep during which any error sets `TBRE_STATUS.sweep_err` is not counted")
|error at end |an error in the cycle `active` clears |4, 5, 4
|===

A start written while the engine is active never reaches the engine (rule R2 of contract C20): its
effect, none, is the CSR testing's (<<tp_csr>>).

*Edge cases:* _count wraps_, the wrap of `count` from 2^31^ - 1 to 0. From reset it takes 2^31^
sweeps, so the run lets the counter start at any value (TB architecture, checker 3 uarch D47): every
value is one the counter reaches after enough sweeps, so the run only adds behaviours.

*Never:* a count step at any other cycle; a step of 2; a step for a sweep with an error.

*Run:* V1, with the counter's start value free.

'''

[[tp_tbre_intr]]
==== tbre_intr: the interrupt

*Requirements:* `REQ_TBRE_28`, `REQ_TBRE_30`, `REQ_TBRE_31`.

*Rule:* a set request for `INTR_STATE.tbre_done` in the cycle the engine stops being active, and in
the cycle software writes 1 to `INTR_TEST.tbre_done`; no set request in any other cycle;
`intr_tbre_done_o(t)` is `INTR_STATE and INTR_ENABLE` of cycle `t - IntrLat`, where `IntrLat` is
0 or 1 and one value for the whole trace ([CIP] Event-type waveform shows an output flop; the
spec fixes the window, not the value, so the check holds for either fixed latency and a one-cycle
pulse is never lost). That `INTR_STATE` stays set until software writes 1 to it, and that such a
write wins in the cycle a sweep ends (`REQ_TBRE_29`), is register file behaviour: <<tp_csr>>.

*Observed at:* the interrupt logic's set request into the register file, the register file's
`INTR_STATE`, `INTR_ENABLE` and `INTR_TEST` outputs, `intr_tbre_done_o`.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|sweep end or test sets |forward |a set request in the cycle `TBRE_REGWEN` rises, and in the cycle of
an `INTR_TEST` write of 1 (`REQ_TBRE_28`)
|set only on end or test |backward |a set request only in such a cycle (`REQ_TBRE_30`)
|line follows state |forward, backward |in every cycle, `intr_tbre_done_o` equals `INTR_STATE and
INTR_ENABLE` of `IntrLat` cycles before, `IntrLat` a free constant held at 0 or 1 for the whole
trace (`REQ_TBRE_31`). Witness: a one-cycle pulse of `INTR_STATE and INTR_ENABLE` with the line
never rising fails for both values
|===

*Cases:* _end, enabled_, a sweep ends with `INTR_ENABLE` set; _end, disabled_, with it clear;
_test write_, an `INTR_TEST` write of 1; _test at end_, an `INTR_TEST` write in the cycle a sweep
ends; _end with error_, a sweep ending with an error; _line next cycle_, `intr_tbre_done_o` rising
the cycle after `INTR_STATE` and `INTR_ENABLE` are both set.

*Never:* a set request with no sweep end and no `INTR_TEST` write; `intr_tbre_done_o` high more
than `IntrLat` cycles after `INTR_STATE and INTR_ENABLE` fell.

*Run:* V1.

'''

=== Sweep

==== How it works

*Rule:* [ToO] Revocation Engine, "the engine sweeps `min(TBRE_NUM_CAPS, (top - TBRE_BASE_ADDR) /
8)` capabilities ... A sweep therefore never leaves the tagged region it starts in."

[cols="1,2,1,1,4",options="header"]
|===
|Sweep |`BASE` |`NUM` |`N` |What it shows

|S1 |`0x1001_FFF0` |4 |4 |crosses from the 128 KiB main SRAM into the second SRAM: one region
|S2 |`0x1002_FFF0` |5 |2 |reaches the top `0x1003_0000` and ends there
|S3 |`0x301F_F5F8` |1 |1 |the last capability below the emulated OTP pages, which read with an
error
|S4 |`0x1003_0000` |1 |- |outside the tagged regions: ignored start
|===

'''

[[tp_tbre_sweep]]
==== tbre_sweep: exactly the swept words are read

*Requirements:* `REQ_TBRE_13`, `REQ_TBRE_14`, `REQ_TBRE_15`, `REQ_TBRE_16`, `REQ_TBRE_40`.

*Rule:* while active, `tbre_tl_h` carries a full-word `Get` of `c` and of `c + 4` for every `c` in
`Swept`, and nothing else; at most two reads are outstanding, with different `a_source`; every read
reaches the engine's tag filter with the hint.

*Observed at:* `tbre_tl_h`; the engine's tag filter's device port (the hint).

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|sweep read carries valid integrity |forward |every sweep read presented on the port carries a valid command integrity (`REQ_TBRE_40`; nothing else checks it: the TL-UL ABVIP leaves every integrity field free)
|both words read |forward |a tracked capability, `BASE + 8k` with `k < N` chosen by the solver at
the start, has both words read, a full-word `Get` of each taken on `tbre_tl_h`, before
`TBRE_REGWEN` rises (`REQ_TBRE_13`)
|Gets inside sweep |backward |every request on `tbre_tl_h` is a full-word `Get` with `BASE \<= a <
BASE + 8N`, presented while active (`REQ_TBRE_14`)
|at most two outstanding |forward |at most two reads outstanding on `tbre_tl_h`; an outstanding
read's `a_source` is not reused (`REQ_TBRE_15`; the second part is the TL-UL ABVIP's rule TL08 on
that port)
|Gets carry hint |forward |the hint is set on every `Get` at the engine's tag filter
(`REQ_TBRE_16`)
|===

*Cases:* _across seam_, sweep S1, across the seam; _clipped at top_, S2, clipped at the top; _below
OTP pages_, S3; _one capability_, `N` = 1; _tracked first_, _tracked in middle_ and _tracked last_,
the tracked capability first in its sweep, in the middle and last (the same covers as
`tbre_status`); _two in flight_, two reads in flight.

*Edge cases:* _last SRAM word_, the last word of the main SRAM region, `0x1002_FFFC`, read; _last
NVM word_, the last NVM word, `0x301F_FFFC`, read; _NVM top_, the end of an NVM sweep near the top,
`BASE` `0x301F_FFF0`, `NUM` 4, `N` 2. The first words past each region, `0x1003_0000` and
`0x3020_0000`, are never read: _Gets inside sweep_. A sweep of the whole NVM (`N` = `0x4_0000`) is
too long to end in a bounded run, so its end is covered with a `BASE` near the top (_NVM top_).

*Never:* a read below `BASE`, at or above `BASE + 8N`, or outside the region; a write or a sub-word
read on `tbre_tl_h`; a third outstanding read; a read while inactive; a read without the hint.

*Run:* V1. Whether a sweep "continued after the top of memory" is observable here: _Gets inside
sweep_ checks every request on `tbre_tl_h`.

'''

[[tp_tbre_done]]
==== tbre_done: every sweep ends

*Requirements:* `REQ_TBRE_37`.

*Rule:* after a taken start, `TBRE_REGWEN` eventually returns to 1, given `xbar_main`, the bitmap
port and the RMW filter answer.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|sweep ends |liveness |after a taken start, `TBRE_REGWEN` is 1 again, at some point
(`REQ_TBRE_37`)
|===

*Cases:* _one-capability sweep_, a sweep of one capability ends; _sweep with clear_, a sweep with
a clear; _sweep with read error_, a sweep with a read error.

*Run:* the liveness run "3 Revocation, liveness B", with assumption A10 and contracts C1, C2. The
engine's clears pass the real 2:1 tag arbiter, so the sweep ends only if the arbiter never starves
input 1: Q15.

'''

=== Decision and clears

==== How it works

*Rule:* [ToO] Revocation Engine, "The TRVK filter applies the load barrier: a tagged capability that
is not a sealing capability and whose base has its revocation bit set is revoked, and so is one
whose bitmap lookup fails. For every revoked capability the engine clears the tag through its tag
filter".

.How the engine decides, for one swept capability
image::cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan_figures.svg#fig4[Revocation decision,align=center,width=700,height=1066]

[cols="1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Step |What happens

|1 |A sweep read answered with `d_error` ends the decision: no clear, `sweep_err` (`tbre_errors`).
|2 |An untagged capability, a sealing capability, or one whose base lies outside the main SRAM is
kept: no lookup is needed, and none is made for a base outside the main SRAM.
|3 |Otherwise the engine reads the bitmap word of its base. A failed lookup counts as revoked, and
also sets `sweep_err` and raises the alert.
|4 |A set bit means revoked.
|5 |A revoked capability is cleared, unless a core write touched it in its watch window
(`tbre_watch`).
|===

*Which lookup is a capability's:* the TRVK filter decodes the base from both words, so it can look
up the bit only once W1's answer has reached it, and it applies the load barrier to that answer
before it passes it on. The checks therefore take the lookup presented while the TRVK filter holds
the capability's W1 answer, from its arrival on the TRVK filter's downstream port to its departure
on the engine's read port, as the lookup for that capability (DV reading).

'''

[[tp_tbre_decision]]
==== tbre_decision: which capabilities are revoked

*Requirements:* `REQ_TBRE_17`, `REQ_TBRE_18`, `REQ_TBRE_19`, `REQ_TBRE_20`, `REQ_TBRE_41`.

*Rule:* for a swept capability `c` read without error: a lookup of `RevWord(Base(c))` is made if
`Tag(c) and not Sealing(c) and Revocable(Base(c))`, and none if `not Revocable(Base(c))`; a clear
for `c` is presented if and only if `Revoked(c)` and no core write touched `c` in its watch window.

*Observed at:* `tbre_tl_h` (the capability's words), the TRVK filter's downstream port (`Tag(c)`,
W1's arrival), the engine's read port (W1's departure), the bitmap port, the engine's clear port.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|lookup carries valid integrity |forward |every lookup presented on the port carries a valid command integrity (`REQ_TBRE_41`; nothing else checks it: the TL-UL ABVIP leaves every integrity field free)
|lookup when needed |forward |a tracked capability read without error that needs a lookup has a
full-word `Get` of `RevWord(Base(trk))` presented on the bitmap port while the TRVK filter holds
its W1 answer (`REQ_TBRE_17`; DV reading, gap, raised with the designers)
|no lookup outside main SRAM |backward |no lookup is presented while the TRVK filter holds the W1
answer of a tracked capability whose base lies outside the main SRAM (`REQ_TBRE_18`; gap, raised with the designers)
|lookup is bitmap Get |backward |every lookup, whatever the capability, is a full-word `Get` of a
word of the bitmap, `0x1100_0000 \<= a < 0x1100_0C00`, presented while the TRVK filter holds a W1
answer that has had no lookup yet (`REQ_TBRE_17`, `REQ_TBRE_18`; DV reading, gap, raised with the designers)
|revoked gets cleared |forward |when the sweep ends, a tracked capability read without error,
revoked and not touched in `Watch(trk)` has had its clear presented (`REQ_TBRE_19`; gap, raised with the designers)
|clear only if revoked |backward |every clear presented on the engine's clear port lies in a swept
capability; for the tracked one, when it is tagged, its decision is known when the clear is
presented and is revoked (`REQ_TBRE_20`; gap, raised with the designers). An untagged tracked capability is outside
this check: rows 1-8 below have no rule
|===

.Truth table: `Tag`, `Sealing`, base region and revocation bit, with the lookup answered without error; one cover per row
[cols="1,1,1,1,1,2",options="header"]
|===
|Row |`Tag(c)` |`Sealing(c)` |`Revocable(Base(c))` |`RevSet(c)` |Clear

|1 |0 |0 |0 |0 |no rule
|2 |0 |0 |0 |1 |no rule
|3 |0 |0 |1 |0 |no rule
|4 |0 |0 |1 |1 |no rule
|5 |0 |1 |0 |0 |no rule
|6 |0 |1 |0 |1 |no rule
|7 |0 |1 |1 |0 |no rule
|8 |0 |1 |1 |1 |no rule
|9 |1 |0 |0 |0 |no, and no lookup
|10 |1 |0 |0 |1 |no, and no lookup
|11 |1 |0 |1 |0 |no
|12 |1 |0 |1 |1 |*yes*
|13 |1 |1 |0 |0 |no
|14 |1 |1 |0 |1 |no
|15 |1 |1 |1 |0 |no
|16 |1 |1 |1 |1 |no
|===

* Each row is one cover of the _truth table row_ family: 16 covers.
* Rows 1-8: an untagged capability has no tag to lose; the spec neither asks for a clear nor
  forbids one, so these rows are covers only, and _clear only if revoked_ excludes them.
* `RevSet` is the bit the word at `RevWord(Base(c))` holds; where no lookup is made, rows that
  differ only in it show that the bit does not matter.
* A failed lookup turns row 11 into a clear (`tbre_errors`).

.Cases: one parameter varied at a time
[cols="2,3,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Held |Varied |Expected clear

|bitmap word and parity |tagged, not sealing, base revocable |bitmap word `0x0000_0000`,
`0xFFFF_FFFF`, `0xAAAA_AAAA`, `0x5555_5555`, each with the base on an even bit and an odd bit: one
cover per word `w` and bit parity `o` |`RevSet(c)`
|permission set |tagged, base revocable, bit set |`p`: memory read-write, read-only, write-only,
data only; executable; sealing with only SE, only US, only U0; all three: one cover each
|`not Sealing(c)`
|no permissions |tagged, base revocable, bit set |`p = G 00000` (no permissions) |gap, raised with the designers;
proposed yes
|base at edge |tagged, not sealing, bit set |one cover per base: `0x1000_0000`, `0x1002_FFF8`, `0x1001_FFF8`,
`0x1002_0000` (main SRAM); `0x3000_0000` (NVM); `0x0FFF_FFF8`; `0x1003_0000` and `0x1003_8000`
(just above the main SRAM); `0x4000_0000` (a peripheral) |`Revocable(Base(c))`
|sealed capability |tagged, not sealing, base revocable, bit set |`otype` not 0: a sealed memory
capability |yes
|===

*Extensions, without a combinatorial explosion:*

* *Base offset in the granule:* bases `0x1000_4000` (_granule offset 0_) and `0x1000_4007`
  (_granule offset 7_) both use bit 0 of word `0x1100_0100`.
* *Base, not address:* the capability of <<defs_capability>> with address `0x1000_4210` and base
  `0x1000_41F0`: the decision follows bit 30 of `0x1100_0104` (the base), not bit 2 of
  `0x1100_0108` (the address). _Base bit set_, base bit set with address bit clear; _base bit
  clear_, the reverse.
* *Decode corrections:* _base correction_, one cover each for `c_b = 0` and `c_b = -1`; _exponent_,
  one cover each for `E` = 0, 4, 14 and 15 (`e` = 24).
* *Where the capability is stored:* _stored in NVM_, a capability stored in the NVM with a main SRAM
  base, which is revocable.

*Never:* a lookup for a base outside the main SRAM; a lookup outside the bitmap; a clear for a
tagged capability that is not revoked (sealing, base outside the main SRAM, or bit clear); a clear
outside the sweep; a decision taken from the address instead of the base.

*Run:* V1. The testbench decodes `Base` and `Sealing` from the ISA (TB architecture D13).

*Blocked by:* Q17 for _no permissions_; Q18 for _no lookup outside main SRAM_; Q41 for _lookup when
needed_ and _lookup is bitmap Get_.

'''

[[tp_tbre_clear]]
==== tbre_clear: the clear and the engine's tag filter

*Requirements:* `REQ_TBRE_21`, `REQ_TBRE_22`, `REQ_TBRE_23`.

*Rule:* the clear of `c` is one tag write of tag 0 to `TagWord(c)`, `TagBit(c)` on input 1 of the
2:1 tag arbiter, at most one per capability per sweep; the engine's tag filter meets the
`REQ_TF_*` read rules on its own ports; a write to it issues one meta request and no host request
and is answered once with the meta answer's error.

*Observed at:* the engine's tag filter's device, host (`tbre_tl_h`) and meta ports.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|clears tracked bit once |forward |the tracked capability's clear leaves on arbiter input 1 as a
write of tag 0 to `TagWord(trk)`, bit `TagBit(trk)`, and no second clear of it follows in the
sweep (`REQ_TBRE_21`; gap, raised with the designers)
|writes tag 0 |backward |every write the engine's tag filter presents on arbiter input 1 carries
tag 0 (`REQ_TBRE_21`)
|tag filter checks hold |both |the `tf_*` checks of checker 1, on the engine's tag filter, through
the shared tag filter model with this instance's configuration: no WTRC, tag-only writes
(`REQ_TBRE_22`; checker 3 uarch D40)
|write answered once |forward |a write presented at the engine's tag filter's device port makes one
meta request and no request on `tbre_tl_h`, and is answered once, `AccessAck`, with the meta
answer's `d_error` (`REQ_TBRE_23`; gap, raised with the designers)
|===

*Cases:* _SRAM capability_, a clear of a capability stored in the main SRAM; _NVM capability_, one
stored in the NVM, for example at `0x3000_0400`, base `0x1000_4000`: clear at word `0x1100_0C10`,
bit 0; _last SRAM capability_, the last capability of the main SRAM region, word `0x1100_97FC`, bit
31; _last NVM capability_, the last NVM capability a sweep can read, `0x301F_F5F8`; _clear answer
error_, a clear answered with `d_error` (`tbre_errors`); _between reads_, a clear answered between
the two reads of the next capability (it covers `REQ_TF_11b` on this tag filter).

*Never:* a clear on `tbre_tl_h`; a second clear for one capability in one sweep; a clear writing
tag 1.

*Run:* V1.

*Blocked by:* Q2 for `TagBit`; Q19 for _write answered once_.

'''

=== Core write watch

==== How it works

*Rule:* [ToO] Revocation Engine, "The watch starts when the engine presents the read of the
capability's lower word, and a capability written from then on until its clear is presented is not
cleared. From the presentation of the clear until it reaches the RMW filter, a core write to the
same capability marks the clear stale, and the RMW filter then only reads the tag word instead of
clearing the tag. Once the clear is at the RMW filter, the socket in front of the RMW filter holds
it there, so no core write reaches the RMW filter before it."

The engine presents its reads on its own read port, in front of its TRVK filter, and its clears on
its own clear port, in front of the socket that merges them with the TRVK filter's reads ([ToO]:
"a socket merges its downstream port with the engine's tag clears in front of the tag filter"). The
TRVK filter and the socket can hold a read or a clear for a cycle or more, so the windows start and
end at the engine's ports, not at `tbre_tl_h` or the arbiter (DV reading).

[cols="1,3,1,4",options="header"]
|===
|Window |From, until |Write |What a core write that touches the capability in it does

|`Watch(c)` |the read of W0 is presented on the engine's read port (cycle 1), until the cycle
before the clear is presented on the engine's clear port (cycle 6) |A |no clear is presented
(`REQ_TBRE_24`)
|`Stale(c)` |the clear is presented (cycle 6), until the cycle before it reaches the RMW filter
(cycle 9): here the socket and then the arbiter hold it |B |the clear reaches the RMW filter as a
read (`REQ_TBRE_25`)
|held |the clear is at the RMW filter (cycle 9), until it is accepted (cycle 10) |C |the write
reaches the RMW filter only after the clear, which stays presented (`REQ_TBRE_27`)
|===

Writes A, B and C are three separate cases, one per window; each touches `c`. The timing is one
example; the tool tries every one. The cycle the clear reaches the RMW filter belongs to the held
window: "Once the clear is at the RMW filter, the socket ... holds it there" (checker 3 uarch D43).

'''

[[tp_tbre_watch]]
==== tbre_watch: a capability the core writes keeps its tag

*Requirements:* `REQ_TBRE_24`, `REQ_TBRE_25`, `REQ_TBRE_26`, `REQ_TBRE_27`.

*Rule:* a touch in `Watch(c)` means no clear for `c`; a touch in `Stale(c)` means the RMW filter
receives a read of the tag word instead of the clear; with no touch, the clear reaches the RMW
filter as a write of tag 0; a clear presented at the RMW filter stays presented, unchanged, until
accepted.

*Observed at:* `cored_tl_d` (the core's writes), the engine's read and clear ports, the 2:1 tag
arbiter's output and the RMW filter's upstream port.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|clear only if untouched |backward |the tracked capability's clear is presented on the engine's
clear port only if no core write touched it in `Watch(trk)` (`REQ_TBRE_24`)
|stale clear becomes read |forward |the tracked capability's clear, touched in `Stale(trk)`,
reaches the RMW filter as a `Get` of the same word and bit (`REQ_TBRE_25`)
|fresh clear stays write |forward |the tracked capability's clear, not touched in `Stale(trk)`,
reaches the RMW filter as the arbiter forwards it: a write of tag 0 (`REQ_TBRE_26`)
|clear held unchanged |stable |every clear at the RMW filter that is not accepted is presented
again in the next cycle, every field the same, before and after the squash (`REQ_TBRE_27`)
|===

.Cases: what touches the capability `c` = `0x1000_1238`
[cols="2,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Core write |Touch?

|word store to W1 |`sw` to `0x1000_123C` (W1 of `c`) |yes
|byte store |`sb` to `0x1000_123B` |yes
|capability store W0 |`csc` W0 to `0x1000_1238` |yes
|capability store W1 |`csc` W1 to `0x1000_123C` |yes
|next capability written |`sw` to `0x1000_1240`, the next capability |no: the clear proceeds
|write not yet accepted |a write presented but not yet accepted |yes
|answered inside window |a write accepted before the watch started and answered inside it |yes,
until answered
|answered before window |a write answered before the watch started |no
|===

.Cases: when the touch happens
[cols="2,5,3",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Cycle of the touch |Result

|touch with W0 read |the cycle the read of W0 is presented on the engine's read port |no clear
|touch just before clear |the last cycle before the clear is presented |no clear
|touch with clear |the cycle the clear is presented |the clear becomes a read
|touch at arrival |the cycle the clear reaches the RMW filter |held: the clear stays a write, and
the write reaches the RMW filter after it
|touch while held |while the clear is held at the RMW filter |the write reaches the RMW filter after
it
|===

*Edge cases:* _two in flight_, two capabilities in flight, the write touching one of them; _write
withdrawn_, a write presented and withdrawn before it is accepted (checker 3 has no hold assumption
on `cored_tl_d`: the spec watches "every write the core presents").

*Never:* a clear for a capability touched in its watch window; a stale clear reaching the RMW filter
as a write; a held clear displaced or changed; a clear turned into a read with no touch.

*Run:* V1; the core's tag filter is cut, its answers and meta requests bound by contracts C6 and C7.

*Blocked by:* Q40 for the windows' ends.

'''

=== Errors

[[tp_tbre_errors]]
==== tbre_errors: what fails a sweep and what raises the alert

*Requirements:* `REQ_TBRE_32`, `REQ_TBRE_33`, `REQ_TBRE_34`, `REQ_TBRE_35`, `REQ_TBRE_36a`.

*Rule:* [ToO] Error Handling, the four rows of the engine:

[cols="4,2,1,1,1",options="header"]
|===
|Cause |The capability |`sweep_err` |`fatal_fault` |Requirement

|`d_error` on a sweep read on `tbre_tl_h` |no clear |1 |0 |`REQ_TBRE_32`
|integrity fault on an answer on `tbre_tl_h` |- |1 |1 |`REQ_TBRE_33`
|`d_error` on the answer to a tag read or a clear |- |1 |1, from the RMW filter |`REQ_TBRE_33`
|`Malformed` answer on `tbre_tl_h` |- |1 |1 |`REQ_TBRE_33`
|`d_error`, integrity fault or `Malformed` on a bitmap lookup |counted as revoked |1 |1
|`REQ_TBRE_34`
|RMW filter fault while active |- |1 |1 |`REQ_TBRE_35`
|===

`sweep_err` is set by nothing else (`REQ_TBRE_36a`). That it stays set until software writes 1 to
it (`REQ_TBRE_36b`) is register file behaviour: <<tp_csr>>.

* *An error on the answer to a tag read or a clear* comes from the meta SRAM, through the RMW
  filter: a device error on the tag path, for which the RMW filter raises `fatal_fault` ([ToO]
  Error Handling: "Device error on the tag path ... `fatal_fault` alert"). Checker 1 checks that
  alert (`tag_alerts`); checker 3, where the RMW filter is a blackbox, checks `sweep_err` for it.
* *An integrity fault or a malformed answer from the RMW filter* is no stimulus: checker 1 proves
  the RMW filter's answers well formed, and a broken meta SRAM integrity raises its own fault
  (`REQ_TAG_08`), which `REQ_TBRE_35` turns into `sweep_err`.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|read error, no clear |forward |a `d_error` on the answer to a read of the tracked capability on
`tbre_tl_h` means no clear for it (`REQ_TBRE_32`)
|cause sets sweep error |forward |each cause of the table is followed by a `sweep_err` set
request, at some point (`REQ_TBRE_32`-`REQ_TBRE_35`; no bound in the spec, P7)
|error set next cycle |forward |that set request comes no later than the cycle after the cause, so
a read of `TBRE_STATUS` once the sweep has ended sees it (DV reading, gap, raised with the designers)
|bad answer raises fault |forward |an integrity fault or (V3) a malformed answer on `tbre_tl_h`,
and any failed bitmap lookup, are followed by one of the engine's fault inputs to the alert, at some
point (`REQ_TBRE_33`, `REQ_TBRE_34`)
|RMW fault raises alert |forward |an RMW filter fault input raised while active raises the alert
request in that cycle (`REQ_TBRE_35`)
|error only for a cause |backward |a `sweep_err` set request comes only while a cause has not had
one yet (`REQ_TBRE_36a`)
|===

That a sweep read's `d_error` raises no alert is checked by `contracts` _engine faults have causes (contract C9)_ (contract C9): the
engine's fault inputs rise only for its listed causes. That a failed lookup counts as revoked is
`tbre_decision` _revoked gets cleared_.

*Cases:* each cause alone: _sweep read error_, a sweep read's `d_error`; _host bad integrity_, a
broken integrity on `tbre_tl_h`; _tag read error_, a `d_error` on a tag read's meta answer; _clear
error_, on a clear's; _bitmap error_, a bitmap `d_error`; _RMW fault_, an RMW filter fault while
active. Then _bitmap bad integrity_, a bitmap answer with a broken integrity; _host malformed
answer_ (run V3), a malformed answer on `tbre_tl_h`; _bitmap malformed answer_ (V3), a malformed
bitmap answer; _error on first capability_, a cause on the first capability of a sweep, _error on
last capability_, on the last; _two causes at once_, two causes in one cycle; _OTP pages read_, a
read error on the emulated OTP pages (`BASE` at `0x301F_F600`, [PG]: "sweeping them results in an
error").

*Edge cases:* _RMW fault while idle_, an RMW filter fault while the engine is inactive: no
`sweep_err` set request (the alert comes from the tag path, `tag_alerts`); _error already set_,
`sweep_err` already set by an earlier sweep.

*Never:* an alert for a sweep read's `d_error`; `sweep_err` with no cause; a failed lookup that keeps
the capability.

*Run:* V1 for errors and integrity faults; V3 for `Malformed` answers, which the TL-UL rules of V1
exclude.

*Blocked by:* Q20 for the RMW filter faults of _cause sets sweep error_ and _RMW fault raises
alert_; Q42 for _error set next cycle_.

[[subsystem]]
== Subsystem-wide and end to end

The alert collects causes from all three checkers, the register file sits in checker 3, and some
requirements follow only from several checkers together. These testpoints close them.

=== Alerts and registers

[[tp_tag_alerts]]
==== tag_alerts: the tag path's faults raise the alert

*Requirements:* `REQ_TAG_07`, `REQ_TAG_08`, `REQ_TAG_10`.

*Rule:* a device error on a meta SRAM answer to the tag path, or an integrity fault (`rsp_intg` or
`data_intg`) on one, requests `fatal_fault`; once raised, the alert stays raised until reset.

*Observed at:* the alert sender's request input; the latch until reset is the sender's own
behaviour, premise P2.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|device error raises alert |liveness |a meta SRAM answer the RMW filter takes with `d_error` raises
the alert request (`REQ_TAG_07`)
|integrity fault raises alert |liveness |a meta SRAM answer the RMW filter takes with a broken
`rsp_intg` or `data_intg` raises the alert request (`REQ_TAG_08`)
|===

`REQ_TAG_10`, the alert staying raised until reset, has no check here: it is premise P2. As for
`wtrc_faults`, the spec gives no time from the fault to the alert, so _device error raises alert_
and _integrity fault raises alert_ have no bound and need no fairness.

*Cases:* _read answer error_, `d_error` on a read's answer; _write Get error_, `d_error` on a
write's `Get`; _write-back error_, `d_error` on a write-back's answer; _bad response integrity_, a
broken `rsp_intg`; _bad data integrity_, a broken `data_intg`; _both integrities bad_, both at
once; _write Get integrity bad_, a write's `Get` answered with a broken integrity and no `d_error`,
the faulty `Get` answer whose write the `rmw_*` checks leave out (<<rmw_tps>>, How it works).

*Never:* a tag path fault with no alert request.

*Run:* V1, checker 1.

'''

[[tp_alert_causes]]
==== alert_causes: the alert only for its listed causes

*Requirements:* `REQ_ALT_04`, `REQ_ALT_05`.

*Rule:* `fatal_fault` is requested if and only if one of the causes of [ToO] Error Handling that
raise it occurs, or software writes `ALERT_TEST`.

.The causes of [ToO] Error Handling, and where each is checked
[cols="5,1,3,2",options="header"]
|===
|Cause |Alert |Requirements |Testpoint

|any meta SRAM access in ePMP mode |no |`REQ_META_04`, `REQ_META_07`, `REQ_ALT_04` |`meta_refuse`
|access outside the region of the requesting port |no |`REQ_META_03`, `REQ_META_07`,
`REQ_ALT_04` |`meta_refuse`
|`PutPartialData` to the meta SRAM |no |`REQ_META_06`, `REQ_META_07`, `REQ_ALT_04` |`meta_refuse`
|device error on the tag path |yes |`REQ_RMW_13`, `REQ_RMW_14`, `REQ_RMW_17`, `REQ_TAG_07`
|`rmw_errors`, `tag_alerts`
|integrity fault on a meta SRAM response |yes |`REQ_TAG_08` |`tag_alerts`
|integrity fault on the CSR interface |yes |`REQ_ALT_01` |`csr` (CSR testing)
|capability store to the NVM that does not match, or whose NVM read fails |no |`REQ_WTRC_04a`,
`REQ_WTRC_08`, `REQ_WTRC_09` |`wtrc_compare`
|capability store to the NVM with a bad integrity, partial, or out of sequence |yes
|`REQ_WTRC_10`, `REQ_WTRC_11` |`wtrc_faults`, bad integrity only; the rest is out of scope
(not covered)
|any other request out of the capability store sequence |yes |`REQ_WTRC_12` |out of scope
(not covered)
|error response to a read of the engine |no |`REQ_TBRE_32` |`tbre_errors`
|any other error, or an integrity fault, on a response to the engine |yes |`REQ_TBRE_33`
|`tbre_errors`
|error, integrity fault or malformed response on a bitmap lookup |yes |`REQ_TBRE_34`
|`tbre_errors`
|RMW filter fault while the engine is active |yes |`REQ_TBRE_35` |`tbre_errors`
|`ALERT_TEST` write |yes |`REQ_ALT_02` |`alert_test` (CSR testing)
|===

*Checks:* the forward direction is in the testpoints of the table. The backward direction, no alert
without a cause, needs the checkers together: checker 1 sees the tag path and WTRC causes with the
engine's and the register file's fault inputs free, checker 3 sees the engine's causes with the RMW
filter's, the WTRC's and the register file's fault inputs free (the register file is a blackbox
there, TB architecture D11). Each proves that its own fault inputs rise only for their causes; two
contracts on those fault signals and the CSR testing close the argument (<<open_questions,proposed
addition P2>>; checker 3 uarch D18).

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|alert only on a fault |backward |checker 3: the alert request is raised only in a cycle where one
of the alert logic's nine fault inputs is raised (`REQ_ALT_05`, the step from the fault inputs to the alert)
|===

*Never:* an alert for a software-reachable cause (the four "no" rows); an alert with no cause.

*Run:* V1 in checkers 1 and 3; composition.

'''

[[tp_alert_test]]
==== alert_test: testing the alert, and locking the test

*Requirements:* `REQ_ALT_02`, `REQ_ALT_03`.

*Rule:* a write of 1 to `ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault` while `ALERT_TEST.regwen` is 1 requests one alert;
once software writes 0 to `ALERT_TEST.regwen`, it reads 0 until reset (`rw0c`: a write of 1 does
not set it again) and `ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault` writes request nothing.

*Cases:* a test write before the lock; the lock; a test write after the lock; a write of 1 to
`regwen` after the lock; a test write in the cycle after the lock.

*Never:* a test alert after the lock; `regwen` back at 1 before reset.

*Run:* the common alert test, `run_alert_test_vseq` in `hw/dv/sv/cip_lib/seq_lib/cip_base_vseq.sv`
(imported by the sim cfg): it writes `ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault`, locks `regwen` at random, reads it
back and expects no alert while locked. It does not write 1 to `regwen` after the lock or test the
cycle after it: those two cases stay open until a directed test adds them. The register file is a
blackbox in checker 3 (TB architecture D11).

'''

[[tp_csr]]
==== csr: register behaviour and the CSR integrity fault

*Requirements:* `REQ_REG_01`, `REQ_REG_02`, `REQ_ALT_01`, `REQ_TBRE_04b`, `REQ_TBRE_05`,
`REQ_TBRE_06`, `REQ_TBRE_29`, `REQ_TBRE_36b`.

*Rule:* every register field resets to its value in [REGS] and behaves as its access type (`ro`,
`rw`, `wo`, `rw1c`, `rw0c`), with `TBRE_REGWEN` gating its three registers; a request on `regs_tl_d`
with a bad command or data integrity requests `fatal_fault`; the register interface takes a request
at most every other cycle (`REQ_REG_02`). In particular: `start_err` and `sweep_err` stay set until
software writes 1 (`REQ_TBRE_04b`, `REQ_TBRE_36b`); writes to `TBRE_BASE_ADDR`, `TBRE_NUM_CAPS` and
`TBRE_START` have no effect while `TBRE_REGWEN` is 0 (`REQ_TBRE_05`); the two registers keep what
software wrote and bits 2:0 of `TBRE_BASE_ADDR` read 0 (`REQ_TBRE_06`); `INTR_STATE.tbre_done` stays
set until software writes 1, and such a write wins in the cycle a sweep ends (`REQ_TBRE_29`).

[cols="2,1,2,3",options="header"]
|===
|Register |Offset |Reset |Access

|`INTR_STATE`, `INTR_ENABLE`, `INTR_TEST` |`0x0`, `0x4`, `0x8` |0 |`rw1c`, `rw`, `wo`
|`ALERT_TEST` |`0xc` |`0x8000_0000` |`fatal_fault` `wo`, `regwen` `rw0c`
|`TBRE_REGWEN` |`0x10` |1 |`ro`
|`TBRE_BASE_ADDR` |`0x14` |0 |`rw`, bits 31:3, gated by `TBRE_REGWEN`
|`TBRE_NUM_CAPS` |`0x18` |0 |`rw`, bits 30:0, gated by `TBRE_REGWEN`
|`TBRE_START` |`0x1c` |0 |`wo`, gated by `TBRE_REGWEN`
|`TBRE_STATUS` |`0x20` |0 |`busy` `ro`; `start_err`, `sweep_err` `rw1c`
|`TBRE_EPOCH` |`0x24` |0 |`ro`
|===

*Observed at:* `regs_tl_d`, and the register file's two sides: `reg2hw` (to the hardware) and
`hw2reg` (from it), free in the register-file unit.

A *good* request is a whole aligned word with valid command and data integrity; the checks claim
nothing for the data of any other request.

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|locked base stable |forward |`TBRE_BASE_ADDR` does not change in a cycle after one with
`TBRE_REGWEN` 0 (`REQ_TBRE_05`; contract C20)
|locked num stable |forward |the same for `TBRE_NUM_CAPS` (`REQ_TBRE_05`; contract C20)
|locked start no strobe |forward |a write to `TBRE_START` while `TBRE_REGWEN` is 0 gives no start
strobe, in its cycle or the next (`REQ_TBRE_05`)
|start strobe only unlocked |backward |a start strobe comes only from a write to `TBRE_START`
while `TBRE_REGWEN` is 1 (contract C20)
|start strobe on write |forward |a good write to `TBRE_START` while unlocked strobes with the bit
written (contract C20)
|base written |forward |a good write to `TBRE_BASE_ADDR` while unlocked lands the cycle after,
bits 31:3 (`REQ_TBRE_06`)
|num written |forward |the same for `TBRE_NUM_CAPS`, bits 30:0 (`REQ_TBRE_06`)
|base changes only by write |backward |`TBRE_BASE_ADDR` changes only in the cycle after a write
to it while unlocked (`REQ_TBRE_06`)
|num changes only by write |backward |the same for `TBRE_NUM_CAPS` (`REQ_TBRE_06`)
|intr set by set request |backward |`INTR_STATE.tbre_done` rises only in the cycle after a set
request (contract C20)
|intr set takes |forward |a set request with no clear in its cycle sets it (contract C20)
|intr stays set |forward |it stays set until software writes 1 to it (`REQ_TBRE_29`)
|intr clear wins |forward |a write of 1 in the cycle of a set request leaves it clear
(`REQ_TBRE_29`)
|read returns register |forward |a good read of `TBRE_BASE_ADDR` (bits 2:0 zero),
`TBRE_NUM_CAPS`, `TBRE_REGWEN` or `TBRE_STATUS.busy` is answered without error with the register's
value; busy holds what the engine last wrote (`REQ_TBRE_06`; contract C20)
|request every other cycle |forward |the register interface takes a request at most every other
cycle (`REQ_REG_02`)
|===

*Cases:* _write while locked_, a good write to each of the three sweep registers while
`TBRE_REGWEN` is 0; _write while unlocked_, the same while it is 1, and a taken start; _lock seen_,
`TBRE_REGWEN` low then high again; _set and clear in one cycle_, an `INTR_STATE` write of 1 in the
cycle of a set request; _status read_, a good read of `TBRE_STATUS` answered with busy set; _sticky
error set and cleared_, a hardware set of `start_err` or `sweep_err` in the cycle software writes 1
to it (software's clear wins, reading Q44; covered, not asserted). The generic CSR tests add a broken command integrity and
a broken data integrity on a register write and on a read, and a write to each register.

*Never:* a start strobe while locked; a sweep register changed by anything but a write to it while
unlocked; `INTR_STATE.tbre_done` set with no set request, or cleared with no write of 1.

*Run:* two parts, both outside the three checkers (TB architecture D11). The register-file unit
(`task_RegFile_Main`, TB architecture, The register-file unit) proves the checks above on the real
register file with everything else cut, so the hardware side is free. The generic CSR tests
(`csr_hw_reset`, `csr_rw`, `csr_bit_bash`, `csr_aliasing`, imported by the sim cfg) check the reset
values and access types (`REQ_REG_01`) and the `rw1c` sticky bits (`REQ_TBRE_04b`,
`REQ_TBRE_36b`). They cannot reach the rows hardware drives: `TBRE_START` is excluded from them
([HJSON] tag `excl:CsrAllTests:CsrExclWrite`) and the simulation testbench runs with CHERIoT mode
off, so no sweep ever starts and `TBRE_REGWEN` is never lowered by hardware. Until
`task_RegFile_Main` runs, every checker 3 result is conditional on contract C20.

'''

=== Mode gating, protocol and environment

==== Mode gating across the subsystem

*Rule:* [HJSON] `MODE_GATING`, "In ePMP mode the entire meta SRAM is inaccessible through all four
ports of the subsystem. No tag lookups are issued."; `INTERSIG.MUBI`: any `cheriot_ena_i` other than
`MuBi4True` (`4'h6`) is ePMP mode.

This is a cross-check, not a testpoint: every row is a case of the testpoint named, and each of
them covers all 16 values of `cheriot_ena_i`.

[cols="4,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Behaviour in ePMP mode |Requirement |Testpoint

|no tag lookup for any access |`REQ_TF_04` |`tf_lookup`
|every load answer untagged |`REQ_TF_11c` |`tf_sticky_tag`
|no capability store to the NVM: a tagged write to the NVM is a plain write |`REQ_WTRC_13`
|`wtrc_store`
|every request on the four requester ports refused with an error |`REQ_META_04`, `REQ_TAG_06`
|`meta_refuse`, `tag_isolation`
|a sweep start ignored, `start_err` set |`REQ_TBRE_02`, `REQ_TBRE_03` |`tbre_start`
|===

'''

[[tp_tlul_protocol]]
==== tlul_protocol: every port follows TL-UL

*Requirements:* none of its own; it checks the protocol every other testpoint relies on.

*Rule:* the TL-UL rules ([TLUL], [TLPC]) on every TL-UL port of a checker, through one instance of
the TL-UL assertion-based VIP (ABVIP), one instance per port: assumed on the ports the testbench
drives, asserted on the ports the design drives; on a link between two of the design's blocks,
asserted on both ends. Asserted, for example: the answers on `cored_tl_d`, `corerevbm_tl`,
`revbm_tl_d` and `regs_tl_d`; the requests on `cored_tl_h`, `tbre_tl_h` and `meta_sram_tl`; the RMW
filter's downstream port (checker 1) and the engine's tag requests (checker 3).

*Also checked:* the answers the subsystem builds itself carry a valid response integrity: the tag
filter's merged-error answers (`REQ_TF_13`), the WTRC's answers (`REQ_WTRC_05`); the access
checkers' error answers have no requirement yet (P1).

[cols="2,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Type |What it checks

|TL-UL rules hold |both |every TL-UL rule of the ABVIP, asserted on each channel the design
drives, on every port of the checker. Checker 1: `cored_tl_d`, `cored_tl_h`, the 2:1 tag arbiter's two inputs, the RMW
filter's upstream and downstream ports. Checker 3: `tbre_tl_h`, the engine's bitmap port, the 2:1
tag arbiter's two inputs, the RMW filter's upstream port, and the engine's four internal links
(read port, TRVK downstream port, clear port, its tag filter's device port; checker 3 uarch U53);
on `cored_tl_d` the testbench plays both ends, so the rules there are only assumed
|===

*Covers:* the ABVIP's own covers, on every port (its uarch doc). They are generic, so a port that
can never do one, by an assumption or by the design, leaves it unreached.

*Run:* V1, every checker.

'''

[[tp_environment]]
==== environment: every assumption can be met

*Requirements:* none of its own; it shows the environment is not empty.

*Rule:* every `assume_` of every checker has a witness cover: a trace in which the assumption holds
and the behaviour it allows happens.

*Cases:* _core two outstanding_, two requests outstanding on `cored_tl_d` (assumption A2); _W1
right after W0_ (assumption A3); _store W0 then W1_, a capability store W0 then W1 (assumption A4);
_every mode value_, each of the 16 `cheriot_ena_i` values (assumption A6), one cover per value;
_host answers in order_, two answers in order on `cored_tl_h` (assumption A7), and _engine read
answers in order_, the same on `tbre_tl_h` (assumption A12); _source top bit_, `a_source` using its
top free bit (assumption A9); _contract witness_, every contract assumed in a run, one cover each.
Checker 3 adds _core answers in order_, two answers in order on `cored_tl_d` from the cut tag filter
(contract C6); _input 0 meta request waits_, a meta request waiting on the 2:1 tag arbiter's input 0
(contract C7); for the rules of contract C20: _start strobe_, a `TBRE_START` strobe, _base address
changes_, `TBRE_BASE_ADDR` changing after a cycle with `TBRE_REGWEN` 1, _interrupt state rises_,
`INTR_STATE` rising after a set request; _core write withdrawn_, a core write presented and then
withdrawn (no hold rule on `cored_tl_d` in checker 3).

*Run:* every run, first: covers before asserts. A cover that becomes unreachable after an assumption
is added means the assumption over-constrains.

'''

*Rule:* each contract of the TB architecture
(xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#contracts[Contracts]) is proven as an assertion in the
checker that holds its logic, and assumed only in the checkers listed there. Each check proves the
contract named in brackets after it.

|Check |Type |What it checks |Proven in

unless the requester withdraws or changes it first ([TL] §5.1, p29: a host may retract a request

are accepted and unanswered, an answer comes; given the meta SRAM accepts and answers and every

*Covers:* one per check, named after the precondition it reaches, in the checker that proves it: a

=== End to end by composition

[[tp_tag_read_after_write]]
==== tag_read_after_write: a tag reads back as written

*Requirements:* `REQ_TAG_01`, `REQ_TAG_02`, `REQ_TAG_03`, `REQ_TAG_04`.

*Rule:* a hinted capability load returns the tag most recently written to that capability through
the tag path; a write sets the tag to its sideband; a tag write changes no other tag.

*Follows from:* the requirements listed in the TB architecture, "End-to-end requirements by
composition", and assumption A11 (the meta SRAM keeps what it is given). No memory is modelled.

*Run:* composition, agreed in review once every requirement it follows from is proven.

'''

[[tp_tag_no_deadlock]]
==== tag_no_deadlock: the core is always answered

*Requirements:* `REQ_TAG_09`.

*Rule:* every core request is answered, whatever the engine's tag filter asks of the shared RMW
filter, given `xbar_main` and the meta SRAM answer.

*Follows from:* `REQ_TF_14`, `REQ_TF_15a`, `REQ_TF_15b`, `REQ_ARB_08`, `REQ_RMW_15`; contracts C1,
C3b.

*Blocked by:* Q15, through `REQ_ARB_08`.

'''

[[tp_rev_end_to_end]]
==== rev_end_to_end: a revoked capability loses its tag, a rewritten one keeps it

*Requirements:* `REQ_TBRE_38`, `REQ_TBRE_39`.

*Rule:* after a sweep with no `sweep_err`, every swept capability that was revoked when read and not
touched in its watch window reads back untagged until written again; a capability touched in its
watch window keeps the tag the core's write gave it.

*Follows from:* checker 3: the clear of a revoked capability reaches the RMW filter as a write of
tag 0 to its bit, and a touched one is never cleared or reaches it as a read (`REQ_TBRE_19`,
`REQ_TBRE_21`, `REQ_TBRE_24`-`REQ_TBRE_27`); checker 1: the arbiter forwards it unchanged and the
RMW filter writes only that bit, and writes nothing for a read (`REQ_ARB_01`, `REQ_ARB_03`,
`REQ_ARB_04`, `REQ_RMW_03`, `REQ_RMW_06`, `REQ_RMW_07`, `REQ_RMW_16`); checker 2: the tag port
forwards it unchanged (`REQ_META_01`, `REQ_META_02`); assumption A11.

*Run:* composition.
